m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which statements describe the plate setup taught in the January 2026 Foundations Learning Guide?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Position the eyes just inside the inside edge of the plate, rather than using the inside ear as the alignment reference.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Use Good Pelvic Alignment (GPA), with the navel pointing between the centre of the front of home plate and no farther than the outside front corner.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Use a balanced stance with the feet about shoulder-width apart or more, adjusting the width to suit the umpire to see the strike zone from the batters sternum, knee, inside and outside edge.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: All of the above.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide changes the slot alignment reference from the inside ear to the eyes just inside the plate edge, explicitly teaches GPA, and revises the stance-width recommendation. Pelvic alignment itself was already described in the earlier manual; the GPA label and fuller instruction are additions.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: You are working from a close runner-on-base starting position when a force play develops. Which first movement best follows the added guidance in the January 2026 Foundations Learning Guide?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move diagonally toward the base to retain the same close working distance.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move at right angles or more to the baseline to create working distance and open the viewing angle as necessary keeping all four essential elements in view.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay in the starting position because a force play should be judged from the same distance as a tag play.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move closer until the base fills your field of vision.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The added instruction focuses on the movement path. A first movement at right angles or more to the baseline creates distance and improves visual separation. Moving diagonally toward the base largely preserves the close tag-play distance.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A wild throw draws the first baseman toward home plate for a possible swipe tag. You are the responsible Base Umpire, but your view of the tag is blocked. Which procedure follows the January 2026 Foundations Learning Guide?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Ask for help before making a call and automatically transfer the decision to the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner out because the ball reached the fielder before the runner reached the base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move dynamically to keep all four essential elements in view where possible. Make a decision on the play, then consult the entire crew if help is needed; do not pass the call to another umpire unless certain they have all the information needed for the entire call.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Leave the play uncalled until a coach requests a conference.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The responsible umpire should make a decision and then consult the crew if needed. A partner may have seen the tag but missed another part of the play, so the call should not simply be transferred. Never guess an out.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A called third strike is not caught. First base is occupied and there is one out. Which communication follows the explicit third-strike guidance in the January 2026 Foundations Learning Guide?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Clearly call "Strike three... Out!" and reinforce the out call if the batter starts toward first base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Give only the strike signal and leave the players to determine whether the batter is out.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "No catch" and direct the batter to first base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for the defense to appeal before declaring the batter out.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With first base occupied and fewer than two outs, the batter is automatically out on the third strike even if it is not caught. The guide expressly requires clear communication of the strike and the out, including reinforcement if the batter starts toward first base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: There are two outs. A runner is approaching home plate while another runner faces a tag play at a different base. What preferred additional verbal communication does the January 2026 Foundations Learning Guide recommend for the Base Umpire?

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Delay all verbal communication until after checking the scoring runner.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Say "Tag" loudly at the exact point of the tag to help the Plate Umpire judge the timing, then complete the ruling after judging control of the ball. The Plate Umpire will point to home plate and signal with one finger if the umpire judges the run scored, or use the arms crossed over the shoulders for no run scores.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "Out" as soon as the glove touches the runner, before judging possession.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Announce whether the run counts from the base where the tag occurs.

m01-mkc.title: m01-mkc.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide recommends an immediate, loud "Tag" cue at the point of contact. This helps the Plate Umpire compare the tag with the touch of home plate while the calling umpire judges ball control. The cue does not by itself declare an out; if the runner is safe, use the safe signal and verbal call as required.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A runner is advancing from first to second on a tag play. Your view is nearly directly over second base, causing the ball, fielder, runner and base to appear lined up. What adjustment follows the guide?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move closer until the base is directly below your eyes.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Work just short of the leading edge, with a slight angle and enough depth to keep the Four Essential Elements visually separated.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly into line with the throw and remain there.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the same position and judge the play mainly from the sound of the catch.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Working just short of the leading edge, with an appropriate angle and depth, keeps the elements visually separated and helps you judge the timing of the tag and the touch of the base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a developing tag play, you reach a good observation position but the fielder then moves across your sightline. How should you use the observation and calling positions described in the guide?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Treat the observation position as a fixed spot and make the call from there.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to the holding zone and call from there.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain at the original spot and assume the tag was applied.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the observation position to read the developing play, then adjust to a calling position that gives an unobstructed view before signaling.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The observation position is an area from which to read the play, not necessarily the final calling position. Adjust as the play develops so you can see the complete action before signaling.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a tag play, the nominal 90-degree position leaves the fielder between you and the tag. Which approach follows the guide's treatment of the 90-degree angle?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Use 90 degrees as a reference, then adjust to obtain an unobstructed view of the Four Essential Elements.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the exact 90-degree angle even though the tag is hidden.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly over the base to remove the need for an angle.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the angle and call the runner out if the throw arrives first.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The 90-degree angle is a guideline, not an absolute requirement. Seeing the play clearly takes priority over reaching an exact angle. The earlier manual already required angle adjustments; the 2026 guide makes this reference concept explicit.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: As a runner slides away from a tag and the fielder reaches across, what focus and movement best follow the guide's tag-play instruction?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Watch only the runner's foot and infer the tag from the fielder's reaction.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay fixed even if the fielder hides the glove.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the ball or ball-glove combination into the tag, adjusting in sync with the developing play while keeping the head as still as possible and the other elements in view.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Watch only the glove and ignore the runner's position relative to the base.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide explicitly links movement to the ball-glove combination and tag application. Keep the Four Essential Elements in view, adjust when required, and maintain head and eye focus throughout.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During pre-pitch preparation, you assess the outfielders' depth and ability. A fly ball is then hit into your coverage area with no real likelihood of being caught. What does the added outfield-coverage guidance emphasize?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Go out on every ball hit to the outfield, regardless of catch potential.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the pre-pitch assessment and crew communication to avoid unnecessary going out and preserve effective base coverage, noting on any fly ball that could be caught, trapped or close to the fair foul line or pole umpires must go out.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "No catch" immediately, before the ball lands.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Go out first, then return through another umpire's area while a base play develops.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Section 9.2.1 specifically cautions against going out on balls with no real likelihood of being caught. Read the play, consider designated coverage, and communicate so the crew retains effective outfield and base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A fly ball near the foul line is first touched by an outfielder while the ball is over fair territory. The fielder juggles it, moves into foul territory and drops it. What timing and status follow the guide's first-touch instruction?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for a completed catch before giving any fair or foul indication.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Declare it foul because it was dropped in foul territory.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the fielder's feet at the moment the ball is dropped to determine fair or foul.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Track the ball and observe the ball's position at first touch and indicate fair then; the later drop in foul territory does not change that status.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The added section separates fair/foul timing from catch/no-catch timing. For this fly ball, fair/foul status is determined by the ball's position at first touch, and the indication should not wait for a completed catch.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: At first base, the fielder is clearly off the base well before the throw arrives. The runner reaches first without being tagged. How should you apply the guide's revised emphasis on pulled-foot calls?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.11.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Make the safe ruling with appropriate routine emphasis; reserve the descriptive point and strong "Off" sell for a play that needs that emphasis and explanation.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Always make a vigorous point and loud "Off" call, no matter how obvious the play is.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner out because the ball arrived before the runner.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Avoid making any ruling because the pulled foot was obvious.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The 2026 guide says not to sell an obvious pulled foot unnecessarily. The stronger descriptive mechanic is for a late or close pulled foot where the reason for the safe ruling needs to be clear. Saving this type of mechanic for the best impact, only when required.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During an inning, the Plate Umpire is occupied with substitutions. The ball is dead and extra offensive players gather near home plate with the on-deck batter. What should the Base Umpires do?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for the Plate Umpire to finish before addressing the players.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Allow extra players near the plate because the ball is dead.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Manage the on-deck area and keep the plate area safe, normally with the Base Umpire nearest the offensive dugout taking responsibility and partners adjusting as needed.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Restart play so the extra players will return to the dugout.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The added dead-ball section gives Base Umpires specific responsibilities while the Plate Umpire handles notifications. Use preventive officiating, manage unauthorized players and maintain a safe working area around home plate.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Play has been suspended for lightning. Twenty minutes after the last lightning sighting, thunder is heard again. Under the guide, when may play resume?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Ten minutes later, because the original 30-minute period is nearly complete.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: No sooner than 30 minutes after that thunder, provided there is no later lightning or thunder and resumption is approved under the competition procedures.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately, because thunder without visible lightning does not affect resumption.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: As soon as both head coaches agree to restart.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The 2026 protocol measures the waiting period from the last lightning sighting or thunder heard. Later thunder starts a fresh 30-minute wait. Consult the UIC or tournament officials and apply the competition procedures.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the changing area after the game, you want to question a partner's decision on a difficult play. Which approach follows the guide's crew-debrief guidance?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Raise it publicly with the teams so everyone hears the explanation.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Tell the partner what they did wrong before allowing them to describe the play.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Avoid discussing difficult decisions because a debrief should cover only successful plays.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Allow the partner to share their observations, ask permission before questioning their decision, and discuss the play honestly, respectfully and confidentially with a focus on learning.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The expanded debrief guidance asks umpires to let partners share their observations and seek permission before questioning them. Keep the discussion confidential and constructive, and listen to all perspectives.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A player is removed for a rule violation rather than ejected for misconduct. Which distinction does the Foundations Learning Guide require the crew to recognize?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: A player removed for a rule violation may remain in the dugout and may coach, an ejected person must leave the game and go to the change room or leave the venue entirely.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Both the removed player and an ejected person must remain in the dugout.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: A removed player may continue playing if the coach agrees.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: An ejection applies only to coaches, while removal applies only to players.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide distinguishes ejection from removal. Its stated instruction is that an ejected person leaves the venue; a player removed for a rule violation may remain in the dugout and coach. This does not make the removed player eligible to continue playing.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.16.q
Foundations Learning Guide: You have credible additional information from a partner and, after crew consultation, decide to change your call. What communication sequence does the guide specify?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Announce the new ruling to the spectators first and leave the coaches to ask for details.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Ask both coaches to join the crew discussion before reaching a decision.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Inform the team affected first, give a simple explanation, then clearly communicate the final ruling.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Change the signal without explaining it so play can resume faster.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Crew consultation occurs away from players and coaches. If the call changes, inform the affected team first, explain simply and communicate the final ruling clearly. The consultation must be based on information, not pressure alone.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The DP takes the FLEX player's defensive position and the FLEX leaves the game. What specific confirmation does the guide add to the lineup-management process?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Tell the scorer the team still has ten players because the DP remains in the batting order.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: When the DP plays defence for the FLEX, this is treated like a substitution for the FLEX or the FLEX’s substitute and must be reported to the Umpire. Confirm with the coach and scorer that the team is now playing with nine, as well as recording and reporting the adjustment.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Allow the coach to report the change directly to the scorer without involving the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait until the end of the inning to record whether the FLEX left the game.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: For an adjustment involving the DP or FLEX leaving or resuming the game, the guide explicitly directs the umpire to confirm with the coach and scorer whether the team is playing with nine or ten. Here the FLEX has left, so the team has nine.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: After several demanding pitches, you notice your concentration fading. Which between-pitch routine does the guide recommend to help maintain focus?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay locked in the set position throughout the entire at-bat.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Change your call timing on the next pitch to force yourself to concentrate.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Review the previous pitch mentally while the next pitch is being delivered.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: After completing the call and checking for continuing action, step back, relax, breathe and briefly notice your surroundings, then refocus before the next pitch.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide adds a deliberate cycle of focusing for each pitch and briefly resetting between pitches. The reset follows the completed pitch and call and must not distract from continuing plays by the catcher or runners.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: At a tournament, a coach says a clear violation should be ignored because it is routinely tolerated in the team's domestic competition. What approach follows the guide's WBSC framework?

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Apply the WBSC standard consistently and impartially, addressing clear violations that affect fairness without searching for marginal or trivial technicalities.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Apply the domestic standard used by whichever team is batting.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Relax enforcement for teams unfamiliar with international competition.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Change the standard late in the game to avoid influencing a close result.

m01-mkc.title: m01-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The added framework states that championship play does not vary with domestic enforcement customs. Apply a consistent WBSC standard from the first pitch to the final out, balancing clear enforcement with avoiding over-officiating trivial technicalities.

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - One-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentations - Foundations to Appendix 4

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the One-Umpire System overview, what are the "Four Essential Elements" the umpire should always try to keep in view?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive players, the offensive players, and the base or the area of play

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the runners, the coaches, and the scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher, the catcher, the batter, and the infield

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the fielders, the foul lines, and the dugouts

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the One-Umpire System, what must the umpire do on every hit ball, before making any call?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain behind the plate until the ball is fielded

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Quickly move out from behind the plate and into the infield for the best view of the play

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "Time" immediately to reset the defense

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly to first base regardless of where the ball is hit

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the Conventions section, how is the plate umpire referred to throughout this manual?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Umpire-in-Chief or "UIC"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Home or "HU"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire or "BU"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate or "PU"

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the Plate Umpire Starting Position guidance, how many warm-up pitches are allowed for each pitcher in the first inning and with each new pitcher?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Three

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Seven

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Five

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Ten

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On every hit ball, which side does the manual instruct the plate umpire to exit from behind the catcher?

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The right side, unless the batter is left-handed

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever side is closer to where the ball was hit

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly up the middle, between catcher and batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The left side, even on a left-handed batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - One-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Module 03 - Two-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: There are no runners on base, and the batter hits a routine ground ball to the shortstop. Per the mechanics for "No Runners on Base," where should the plate umpire move to get the best view of the play?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Into foul ball territory toward third base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: With purpose, out in front of home plate towards the pitcher's area

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Straight up the first base line, following the batter-runner

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay behind the catcher and make the call from the plate

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A runner is on third base only, and the batter hits a ground ball to the third baseman. Per the mechanics for "Runner at Third Base," what movement should the plate umpire make?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move into foul ball territory toward third base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move out in front of home plate towards the pitcher's area, as with no runners on base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain stationary behind the catcher

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Sprint directly to first base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With the bases loaded, the batter hits a fly ball to shallow right field. Consistent with the "Bases Loaded" mechanics (which follow the same pattern as Runner at Third Base), where should the umpire move?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Out in front of home plate toward the pitcher's area

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Toward the right field foul line

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly behind second base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Into foul ball territory toward third base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The plate umpire has moved into position for a potential play at first base on a ground ball. What sequence does the manual prescribe for making the call?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Call immediately upon seeing the throw, then confirm with a signal

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Signal first, then verbally call

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Stop… Wait… Call and Signal

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move continuously while calling to keep angle on the play

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A fly ball is hit to the outfield with no runners on base. Before moving toward the base where the play will be made, what must the umpire judge?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Whether the ball is fair or foul only

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner's lead-off distance

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whether the fielder is left- or right-handed

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Catch or no catch

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball has returned to the infield after a play in the outfield, and all play has ceased. What should the plate umpire do, per the manual?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: May call and signal "Time"

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue actively pursuing the play in case a runner attempts another advance

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately return to the dugout area

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Call an automatic conference with the coaches

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and second base, a fly ball is hit to left field that may or may not be caught. Consistent with the One-Umpire System's instruction to give priority in positioning, which runner should most influence the umpire's positioning?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter-runner heading to first base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner on first base

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner on second base (the lead runner)

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever runner is physically closest to the umpire's current position

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A ground ball is hit with a runner on first base. The throw to first base for the batter-runner appears to be a routine, uncontested play, but the runner from first may try to advance on the throw. What does the manual instruct the umpire to do?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay fixed on the play at first base until it is fully completed

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Shift towards where the next play may occur, especially since it is a possible tag play

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "Time" immediately once the throw to first is released

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to the outfield to prepare for the next batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A ground ball is hit sharply down the third base line with a runner on third base. Besides moving into foul ball territory toward third base, what additional responsibility does the manual assign the umpire in this situation?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay close to the line to call fair/foul

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately signal "Out" before the play concludes

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner out for running outside the baseline

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Request assistance from the third base coach

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: While moving with purpose to get into position for a developing play, what positioning principle must the umpire observe, according to the One-Umpire System overview?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Always stand exactly halfway between the two bases involved in the play

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Ensure the chosen position does not put the umpire in the way of a player or a thrown ball

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Always face the pitcher regardless of where the play is developing

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain a fixed distance from the base at all times

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Where does the plate umpire stand between innings in the One-Umpire System?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: At the pitcher's plate, facing home

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind the catcher at all times

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About one third of the way from home plate toward first base in one half inning and toward third base in the other, about 30 cm (12 inches) off the line in foul territory

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: At second base, facing home plate

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire stands facing the diamond with the hands relaxed at the sides, with the mask under the left arm.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Between innings in the One-Umpire System, which side does the plate umpire stand on?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.11.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Always on the third base side

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Always on the first base side

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: On the side of the team going onto the field

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: On the side of the team coming off the field

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire also hustles the teams on and off the field.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: How many warm-up pitches are allowed at the start of each inning after the first inning?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Five

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Two

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Three

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Eight

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Five warm-up pitches are allowed for each pitcher in the first inning and with each new pitcher.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During the warm-up pitches, what should the plate umpire tell the catcher?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: When the second to last warm-up pitch has been thrown

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: When the first warm-up pitch has been thrown

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Nothing; the catcher counts the pitches

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Which pitch is the last, only if asked

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: After the warm-up pitches the umpire sweeps the plate and takes a position behind the catcher.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On every hit in the One-Umpire System, how does the plate umpire exit from behind the catcher?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: By stepping straight backwards

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Via the right, even on a right-handed batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Via the side of the batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Via the left, even on a left-handed batter

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If the ball is close to the foul line the umpire moves to the line and straddles it to make the fair/foul call.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on base, whom does the One-Umpire System say to give priority in the umpire's positioning?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner on third base only

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The lead runner

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The fielder with the ball

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter-runner

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: On every hit the umpire moves out from behind the plate into the infield for the best view of the play that develops.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.16.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What does the One-Umpire System manual say about making a call other than calling balls and strikes?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for the coach to ask

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: You should never make a call without moving out from behind the plate unless at home

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Make calls from behind the plate to stay out of the way

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Make the call before the ball arrives

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The single umpire has no partner to assist, so must move with purpose to get the best possible position to stop and make the call.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Why must the One-Umpire System umpire know where the runners are every time the ball is thrown?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: To signal the coaches

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: To count the number of throws

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To know which base to sweep

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: In case the ball is thrown out of play

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire must also take a quick look at the runners as they touch bases, especially when scoring at home.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Where does the plate umpire carry the mask between innings in the One-Umpire System?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: On the head

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Under the right arm

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Under the left arm

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: In the ball bag

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: During the first half inning and when there is a change of pitchers the umpire may put on the mask to observe the warm-up pitches.

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the One-Umpire System, which calls is the plate umpire responsible for?

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Every call in the game, including illegal pitches, fair/foul balls, batting infractions, and safes and outs

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Only balls and strikes

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Only calls at home plate

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Only fair/foul balls

m01-mkc.title: m02-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: It is obvious that not everything that happens will be seen, so the single umpire must hustle around and inside the diamond for the best position.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - Two-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentations - Foundations to Appendix 4

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the Two-Umpire System manual, which of the following is NOT one of the 'Four Essential Elements' an umpire must keep in unobstructed view?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The scoreboard.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The offensive players.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The defensive players.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The Four Essential Elements are the ball, defensive players, offensive players, and the base or area of play.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Under the Division Principle, and subject to its stated exceptions, which umpire normally takes calls at home plate and third base?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires jointly.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire arrives first.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire normally covers home and third; the Base Umpire normally covers first and second. The stated exceptions modify this division.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the Infield/Outfield Principle, where does the Base Umpire move when the ball is hit to the outfield?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Into the infield

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Further into the outfield, toward the ball

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To a position on the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind home plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With the ball in the outfield, the Base Umpire moves into the infield to keep the play in front.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What is the rationale behind the Leading Runner Principle in the Two-Umpire System?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The lead runner is always the fastest runner on base and needs closer supervision

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire must always start closest to second base regardless of runners

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire positions with the lead runner because the catcher is expected to attempt a pick-off play on that runner

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire delegates lead-runner coverage to avoid fatigue

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The expected pickoff on the lead runner determines the Base Umpire's starting-position priority.

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, what is the Base Umpire's starting position per the manual?

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: 4-5 meters (15 feet) behind the base line, in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly behind the pitcher's plate, facing home plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: 3.5 meters (10-12 feet) behind first base, on the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: 5.5 meters (18 feet) behind first base in foul territory, 150 mm (6 inches) off the line

m01-mkc.title: m03-mkc.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners, the Base Umpire starts about 5.5 meters (18 feet) behind first base in foul territory and 150 mm (6 inches) off the line.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - Two-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Module 04 - Three-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, the batter hits a routine ground ball to shortstop, who throws to first base. Who calls the play at first?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because it is a force play.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is closer to the base.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because the batted ball was fair.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire moves into fair territory, lets the ball turn them into the play, then stops, waits, calls and signals. The Base Umpire has the play at first.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, the batter hits a ground ball that develops into a potential double play. Per the manual, what should the Base Umpire do?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Anticipate the double play, move quickly toward the base where the first play will be made, and call all plays made on the first throw

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain in the ready position at first base until the throw is complete

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately move to third base to cover R1's advance

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Hand off first-base coverage to the Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Anticipate the double play and move toward the base where the first play will occur. Let the ball turn you into the play, then stop, wait, call and signal.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, the batter hits a fly ball to the outfield that is caught. Which umpire is responsible for the tag-up call at first base?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires jointly

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither - tag-ups are not judged on caught fly balls

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner at first and a fly ball to the outfield, the Base Umpire moves inside and takes the tag-up at first. The Plate Umpire judges catch/no catch.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and second, the runner who began on second attempts to steal third on the pitch. Which umpire has the call at third?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because the normal division always applies at third.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is nearest home plate.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire has the clearer angle at that moment.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire, under the stated steal exception.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: A steal from second to third is an explicit exception to the normal division: the Base Umpire makes the call.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on second and third, the batter hits a ball to the outfield. Which complete assignment follows the guide?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire takes the runner who started on second into third and the batter-runner through first, second and third; Plate Umpire watches the tag-up at third and prepares for a play at third or home.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire takes only the batter-runner through first and second; Plate Umpire takes both original runners and the batter-runner at third.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire takes the runner who started on third to home; Plate Umpire takes the batter-runner through all bases.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires follow the runner who started on third and leave the batter-runner to advance without coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Page 27 assigns the original runner from second to the Base Umpire at third, along with the batter-runner through third. The Plate Umpire watches the tag-up at third and anticipates third/home action. Communicate any necessary deviation.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With the bases loaded, a ground ball is fielded and the first throw goes directly home for a force play. Which umpire calls the play at home?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire, because every first throw belongs to the Base Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is nearest the pitcher.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires simultaneously.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, who anticipates and covers the play at home.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire covers home and must anticipate the play there. Do not read the Base Umpire's first-throw assignment as transferring home-plate coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter hits a ball to the outfield and, as the Batter Runner, advances all the way to third base. Under the exceptions to the Division Principle, who takes the call on the Batter Runner at third base?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, since third-base calls always belong to the Plate Umpire under the Division Principle

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire started the play closer to third base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because the Base Umpire only covers first and second base calls

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter-runner advancing to third is an explicit exception to the normal division. The Base Umpire takes the batter-runner through first, second and third.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second base only, and before the pitch, where should the Base Umpire be positioned?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: 5.5 meters (18 feet) behind first base in foul territory

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind and off the second base fielder, shading toward first base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind and off the shortstop, shading toward the runner on second base, with a view of the pitcher, runner and home plate area

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: In the outfield grass behind second base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner at second only, the Base Umpire starts behind and off the shortstop, shading toward that runner, while maintaining a view of the pitcher, runner and home-plate area.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire is set up for a potential play at first base and it becomes clear the throw will require a tag rather than a force. Per the manual, what adjustment should the Base Umpire make?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to approximately 3.5 meters (10-12 feet) to see and make the call

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain at 5.5 meters (18 feet), since that distance applies to all calls

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to 4-5 meters (15 feet) behind the baseline

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Retreat further into foul territory for a wider angle

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide gives approximately 5.5 meters (18 feet) for force plays and 3.5 meters (10-12 feet) for tag plays. Adjust for the tag play while keeping the Four Essential Elements in front.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and third base, a ground ball is hit to the infield. The defense makes the first play (a force at second base), then throws home attempting to get the runner from third. Which umpire is responsible for calling this second, subsequent play at home plate?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire, since the Base Umpire calls all plays including follow-up throws

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires must call it simultaneously

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is positioned in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, who is responsible for succeeding plays at third base or home plate after the first infield play

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: After the first infield play, the Plate Umpire covers succeeding plays at third or home. In this scenario the throw home is the subsequent play.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on first and second, the batter hits a ground ball and the defense makes its first play at third base. Who has that first call at third?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire, because third base always belongs to the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Base Umpire, under the exception for the first infield call on a base.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires must signal.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither umpire until the next throw is made.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The first infield call on a base belongs to the Base Umpire even when it is at third. The Plate Umpire prepares for succeeding plays at third or home.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, a fly ball is hit close to the right-field foul line. What does the guide require of the Plate Umpire?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.11.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay behind the catcher and leave fair/foul and catch/no catch to the Base Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the batter-runner to second and make no ruling on the fly ball.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move toward the flight of the ball, straddle the line for the close fair/foul decision, and judge catch/no catch.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly to third base without watching the ball.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire moves toward the flight of the ball and judges its status. On a hit close to a foul line, straddle the line for the fair/foul decision. The Base Umpire takes the batter-runner through the bases.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A developing play requires you to deviate from the normal division of coverage in the two-umpire system. What must you do?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Communicate the deviation to your partner.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Assume your partner will work out the change without communication.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "Time" immediately on every deviation.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to call every play at both bases yourself.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The exceptions section expressly requires communication when umpires must deviate. Clear communication helps the crew maintain coverage and avoid competing calls.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: As the pitcher assumes the set position, how should the Base Umpire place their feet?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: One foot well ahead of the other

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Together, with the weight on the heels

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: As wide as possible

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: A comfortable distance apart, at least shoulder width, relaxed but still

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: As the pitcher brings the hands together, place the feet a comfortable distance apart, at least shoulder width, and remain relaxed but still. At release, unlock the knees slightly, with weight lightly on the balls of the feet and hands near the belt.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: The batter is left-handed and hits the ball. Which side of the catcher does the guide require the Plate Umpire to use when exiting?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The right side, because the batter is left-handed.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever side leads directly into the catcher's movement.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain behind the catcher until every runner reaches a base.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The left side, including when the batter is left-handed.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide states that on every hit the Plate Umpire exits to the left of the catcher, even with a left-handed batter, then moves to the required position.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners initially on base, the throw to first following an infield hit gets away but remains in play. The batter-runner advances. What should the Base Umpire do next?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain outside first base and leave both second and third to the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Cut into the infield and prepare to take the batter-runner at second and third.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call "Dead Ball" solely because the throw was an overthrow.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the ball into the outfield and abandon the batter-runner.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: On an overthrow following this infield play, the Base Umpire cuts into the infield and prepares for second and third. The scenario states that the ball remains in play.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.16.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What must the Base Umpire NOT do when setting up before the pitch?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stand relaxed

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Face home plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep a clear view of home plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Set up ahead of any infielder before the catcher receives the pitch or the ball is batted

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Before the catcher receives the pitch or the ball is batted, the Base Umpire must not set up ahead of an infielder and must retain an unobstructed view of home plate.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On an infield hit with no runners on base, what does the plate umpire do?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Go to second base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Trail the batter-runner about one third of the way to first base, watching for possible interference or obstruction

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move straight to third base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay behind the plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on an infield hit, the Plate Umpire trails the batter-runner about one third of the way to first, watching for possible interference or obstruction and assisting as needed.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Between innings in the Two-Umpire System, where does the plate umpire stand?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Just off the third base line in foul territory, about one third of the way to third base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Just off the first base line, about one third of the way to first base

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind the catcher

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: At the pitcher's plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Between innings, the Plate Umpire stands in foul territory just off the third-base line, about one third of the way to third. The Base Umpire uses the corresponding position on the first-base side.

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Two-Umpire System, who is responsible for calling illegal pitches?

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire only

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is closer to the pitcher's plate

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires share the responsibility

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The Base Umpire only

m01-mkc.title: m03-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires share responsibility for illegal pitches. The Plate Umpire also has the listed fair/foul and batting-infraction responsibilities; specific pitching responsibilities are developed in the Foundations guide.

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - Three-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentations - Foundations to Appendix 4

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to the Three-Umpire System manual's 'Four Essential Elements', which four things must an umpire maintain an unobstructed view of to keep the play in front of them?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive players, the offensive players, and the base or area of play

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the pitcher, the catcher, and the base

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the runner, the coach, and the scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the fielder, the dugout, and the foul line

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The four elements are the ball, defensive players, offensive players, and the base or area of play.

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Under the general Division Principle, subject to the stated exceptions and specific scenario instructions, which umpire normally takes calls at home plate and third base when a Base Umpire goes out on a fly ball?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining Base Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Whichever umpire is closest to third base

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires jointly

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The general division gives home and third to the Plate Umpire and first and second to the remaining Base Umpire. Apply the stated exceptions and the detailed scenario instructions.

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What does 'clearing the catcher' mean for the Plate Umpire, as described in the Three-Umpire System manual?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Sprinting to the backstop to check for interference

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Signalling the catcher to stand up before every pitch

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Taking a small step to the Plate Umpire's left to move out from behind the catcher

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Moving directly behind the catcher for the best angle

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Clearing the catcher means a small step to the Plate Umpire's left, creating space and opening the view before the play develops.

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the Base Umpire Ready Position described in this manual, when should the umpire adopt the 'ready' position by unlocking the knees slightly and resting weight on the balls of the feet?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: As soon as the pitcher assumes the set position

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: During the pre-game meeting

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Only after the ball is put in play

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: As the pitcher starts the pitch

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The feet are placed comfortably apart when the pitcher sets. As the pitcher starts the pitch, unlock the knees slightly, with weight lightly on the balls of the feet and hands near the belt.

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per the Infield/Outfield Principle in the Three-Umpire System, what should a base umpire who is NOT going out on a fly ball do once the ball is in the outfield?

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move out beyond the base line to back up the play

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain in the ready position at their original base

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate inside the diamond

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the ball toward the outfield fence

m01-mkc.title: m04-mkc.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Base umpires not going out rotate inside when the ball is in the outfield. When an umpire goes out, the remaining Base Umpire must rotate inside.

Foundations Learning Guide: Foundations - Three-Umpire Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, a ground ball is hit to the infield resulting in a possible force play at first base. If the batter-runner is called safe at first and continues toward second base, which umpire has rotated into position to make that call, per the Three-Umpire System manual?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire, trailing the runner to second base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1, staying at first base to also cover second

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U3, rotating to second base in line with the plate umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 remains at third base and does not rotate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 rotates to second, in line with the Plate Umpire, ready for a call if the batter-runner is safe at first and continues to second.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on base, U1 goes out on a fly ball to the outfield. If the ball is not caught, which umpire is responsible for taking the batter-runner into second base and around to third base?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 returns from the outfield to take the runner

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Coverage is shared equally between the Plate Umpire and U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: For this specific scenario, U3 moves inside and takes the batter-runner into second and around to third if the ball is not caught. The Plate Umpire initially assists with a possible first-base play and then prepares for home.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, a ground ball is hit to the infield presenting a potential double play. What does U3 do in anticipation of the throw to second base?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Steps forward towards second base to get an angle on the throw

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Moves to third base to cover a possible advance

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remains in the original ready position off the third base line

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Goes out toward the outfield to back up the throw

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 usually steps forward toward second and adjusts to obtain the best angle for the throw to second. U1 prepares for the subsequent play at first.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second base only, a ground ball is hit to the infield. Which umpire is responsible for calls at both first and second base in this situation?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both U1 and U3 share the calls

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 moves toward the initial play and is responsible for first and second. U3 prepares for the runner advancing from second toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on third base only, a ground ball is hit to the infield. If U3 is unable to release R1 at third base (R1 does not proceed home), which umpire may be required to take the batter-runner to second base and make the call?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3, after releasing third base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire, moving up the first base line

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: No umpire - the play is a dead ball

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If the runner remains at third and U3 cannot release that coverage, U1 may need to take the batter-runner to second. Read the runners and the other umpires' positions.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on third base, U1 goes out on a fly ball. Which umpire moves to the holding zone between home and third base to watch the tag-up of R1, while also preparing for a possible call at home plate?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1, before leaving for the outfield

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: No umpire watches the tag-up in this situation

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire uses the holding zone between home and third to observe the tag-up at third, then moves as needed for a play at third or home. U3 moves inside to cover the batter-runner.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With the bases loaded, U1 goes out on a fly ball within U1's coverage, away from the right-field-line exception. How should the remaining umpires divide tag-up observations?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire watches first and second; U3 watches third.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 watches all three tag-ups while the Plate Umpire watches only the catch.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Plate Umpire watches the tag-up at third; U3 moves inside and watches the tag-ups at first and second.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: No tag-up observations are needed until the ball is caught.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: When U1 goes out in this scenario, the Plate Umpire observes the tag-up at third and prepares for third/home action. U3 moves inside to observe first and second. Observe first touch and the runners' contact with their bases.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on second and third base, a ground ball is hit to the infield. If R1 (the runner on third) advances toward home, what does U3 do, per the manual?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remains at third base regardless of R1's advance

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Follows R1 toward home plate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately rotates to first base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Moves into fair territory about one step in anticipation of a play on R2 progressing from second base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If the lead runner advances home, U3 steps into fair territory to prepare for the runner coming from second. If the lead runner stays at third, U3 retains third-base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first base, the ball is hit through the infield to the outfield and no umpire goes out. As R1 progresses toward second base, where does the Plate Umpire rotate to in preparation for a possible call?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: First base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Third base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire remains at home plate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Second base, alongside U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: As the runner from first progresses to second, the Plate Umpire rotates toward third for a possible call. The crew must also maintain home coverage as the rotation develops.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second base, the ball is hit through the infield toward right field. Per the manual's note, if there is a possibility of a play at third base on the throw-back, what should U3 do?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Release to cover home plate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move back out beyond the base line in fair territory

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain on the foul line even with the base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate inside the diamond

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: On a hit to right or right-center, U3 may read the play from near the line. If a throwback play at third is possible, rotate inside. If the throw is home with no immediate third-base play, the guide allows movement back beyond the baseline in fair territory.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A Base Umpire has gone out and the fly ball is caught. The remaining Base Umpire comes inside the diamond in front of the last runner. Under the stated exception, when may that umpire take the runner into third?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Automatically, without communicating with the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Only if the outfield umpire returns to cover home.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: After communicating that coverage with the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Never; the Plate Umpire must take every runner at third without exception.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: After a caught fly ball, the remaining Base Umpire who comes inside in front of the last runner may take that runner into third, but only after communicating with the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Before turning their back to go out on a fly ball, what should the umpire do?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.11.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Look at their partners, then indicate and verbalise 'going'

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for the plate umpire to call the ball

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Ask the coach

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Run straight out without any signal

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Watch the flight of the ball, make umpire-to-umpire eye contact, then indicate and verbalize "Going" before turning your back to take the fly ball.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In which direction do umpires signal an out on a caught fly ball in the outfield?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Towards the scorer

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Towards home plate

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Towards the ball, after stopping, deciding and communicating

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Towards the dugout

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Stop, decide and communicate. Signal the out toward the ball. Give a no-catch signal for a trapped ball when needed; an obvious no-catch does not require a routine safe signal.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Once an umpire has gone out to the outfield, what must they do?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain in the outfield until all play has ceased, but keep observing infield plays so they can assist if requested

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Return to the infield immediately

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Go to second base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay and look only at the outfield

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire who goes out remains in the outfield until all play has ceased, while continuing to observe infield action in case information is needed in a crew discussion.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Who signals a home run in the Three-Umpire System?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Always the umpire at first base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire nearest the dugout

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Always the plate umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire in the outfield, unless no base umpire moved to the outfield, in which case the plate umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The outfield umpire signals the home run. If no Base Umpire moves to the outfield, that responsibility belongs to the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A base umpire mistakenly does not go out to a fly ball. Who makes the call?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire at second base, if there is one

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The plate umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The coach

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The nearest outfielder

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If a Base Umpire mistakenly does not go out on a fly ball, the Plate Umpire makes the call. Base umpires may assist on trapped balls. This does not require the crew to abandon its remaining coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.16.q
