Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner at third, the runner's lead blocks U3's view of home plate. What starting-position adjustment does the guide permit?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move in front of the shortstop so the runner is behind the umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay directly on the foul line and accept the blocked view.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move behind the catcher to share the Plate Umpire's view.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Work in foul territory behind third, up to about 2 meters (6 feet) off the foul line, to retain an unobstructed view of home plate and the batter.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 must avoid being screened by the runner leading off or returning to third. The wider starting position in foul territory preserves the view needed for dead-ball situations and assistance on checked swings.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: At the pre-game meeting in the Three-Umpire System, where does U1 stand?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Behind the catcher

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: At the infield end of the right-hander's batter's box

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: At the infield end of the left-hander's batter's box, looking towards the back net

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: On first base

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 stands at the infield end of the left-handed batter's box facing the back net. U3 takes the corresponding position at the right-handed batter's box.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: After the third out with no runners on base, who sweeps the pitcher's plate on the way to the base lines?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whoever is closest to the dugout

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The plate umpire

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The closest Base Umpire normally sweeps the pitching plate. With no runners on, or if both Base Umpires are equally distant, U3 takes the responsibility.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a playback tag at first base, the initial position does not give U1 a clear view of the tag and the leading edge. Which adjustment is permitted by the guide?

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain fixed and infer the tag from the runner's reaction.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Adjust to keep the Four Essential Elements in view, including moving into foul territory if necessary while retaining sight of the leading edge.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly behind the fielder so the tag area is hidden.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Ignore the leading edge and watch only the glove.

m01-mkc.title: m04-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The first-base playback is often a swipe tag. The guide permits a foul-territory position when needed to keep the Four Essential Elements in front, but U1 must still see the leading edge. Adjust as the play develops.

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4: Elite Positioning Philosophies

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentations - Foundations to Appendix 4

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 4's Key Concepts and Glossary, what are the 'Four Essential Elements' an umpire must observe together to make an accurate decision?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire's position, the runner's speed, the crowd noise, and the scoreboard

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher, the catcher, the batter, and the plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive player, the offensive player(s), and the base or area of play

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The starting position, the calling position, the focal point, and the leading edge

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In Appendix 4's Key Concepts and Glossary, how is 'Parallax Error' defined?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: A visual distortion that occurs when the umpire views a play from a poor angle that prevents clear separation and timing of the elements of the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: A rule violation that occurs when a pitcher's stepping foot lands outside the pitching lane

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The delay between an umpire seeing a play and signalling a decision

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: A mechanical error caused by starting too far from the base

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Where is the Point of Plate (POP) Position generally located?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Directly on the foul line, level with first base

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Approximately 3-4 metres (10-12 feet) directly behind home plate, aligned with the centre axis of the plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Inside the diamond, halfway between home plate and the pitcher's plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: At the Second Base Diagonal Angle, 3-4 metres behind second base

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What disciplined sequence does Appendix 4 identify as the technique umpires use to avoid anticipation and cognitive bias before making and communicating a decision?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: See - Move - React - Call

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Position - Track - Judge - Signal

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Watch - Wait - Confirm - Announce

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Stop - See - Decide - Signal

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: How does Appendix 4 describe its relationship to Appendix 5?

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4 replaces Appendix 5 for umpires below elite level

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4 and Appendix 5 cover identical content in different formats

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4 provides the why; Appendix 5 will provide the how

m01-mkc.title: m05-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4 is only for trainers, while Appendix 5 is only for umpires

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 4: Elite Positioning Philosophies

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Module 06 - Appendix 5: Elite Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During a bang-bang tag play at third base, the umpire clearly sees the fielder's glove make contact with the runner's leg but does not clearly track whether the runner's hand had already reached the base. The umpire calls the runner out based on the glove contact alone. Which principle from Appendix 4 best explains the risk in this decision-making process?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Anticipatory signalling, because the umpire prepared the signal before the play began

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Affirmation bias, because fixating on the tag action can cause the brain to prematurely confirm an out and override the actual relationship between the ball, runner, and base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax error, because the umpire was positioned too far from the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: A breach of primary responsibilities, because the umpire failed to rotate to the correct base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A sharp line drive travels near the third-base bag. The Plate Umpire, positioned behind the catcher, is the only umpire with a view of the play. Based on Appendix 4's explanation of parallax error, why is this positioning a concern, and what does correct mechanics require?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: It is not a concern, because the Plate Umpire's slot position is aligned with every part of the field

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire should call the play from memory of the pitch location rather than the batted ball

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: It is only a concern for home run judgments, not for line drives near a base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax may make the ball appear fair or foul incorrectly from behind the plate; mechanics require an umpire to be on the foul line to accurately judge the call

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A runner attempting to avoid a swipe tag at second base slides to the back corner of the bag, away from the umpire's position on the Second Base Diagonal Angle. What does Appendix 4 direct the umpire to do in this situation?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain fixed on the Second Base Diagonal Angle regardless of how the play develops, since it is the designated starting reference

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Immediately move to the Point of Plate position to gain a better angle

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Adjust position along the diagonal or move off it as needed, since the priority is always maintaining an unobstructed view of the key elements

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Call time and reposition only after the play has concluded

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a potential tag play, a runner runs directly at the umpire, forcing the umpire to move suddenly to avoid a collision. What does Appendix 4 say this situation indicates?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire was in the wrong position or did not wait for the play to develop properly

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner committed interference and should be called out automatically

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire correctly anticipated the play and should hold their ground next time

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: This is a normal and unavoidable part of elite mechanics requiring no adjustment

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: During a game, the umpire positioned near second base has a clear, obvious view that the pitcher's stepping foot landed completely outside the pitching lane, while the Plate Umpire's angle does not allow a clear view of the violation. According to Appendix 4, what should the umpire near second base do?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Say nothing, because only the Plate Umpire has authority to call an illegal pitch

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait until the next inning to raise the issue with the Plate Umpire privately

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: If certain, call the illegal pitch, since WBSC mechanics permit the umpire near second base to manage the stepping foot when it is completely outside the pitching lane

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Signal the Plate Umpire discreetly but never call the violation directly

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire begins forming their 'out' signal mentally while the fielder is still completing the tag attempt, before the play has fully concluded. According to Appendix 4, what is the likely consequence of this habit?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: It disrupts timing and encourages early calling, because the brain shifts focus away from processing the final elements of the action

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: It has no effect on accuracy, since experienced umpires can multitask effectively

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: It improves reaction time and is a recommended technique for bang-bang plays

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: It only affects balls and strikes calls, not tag plays

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a Four-Umpire system, a fly ball is hit into the gap where both U1 and U2's coverage areas overlap, with U1 also converging on the ball. Which umpire should go out first, per Appendix 4?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 should go out first because U2 has the more central starting position

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires should go out simultaneously to double-cover the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither umpire should go out; the Plate Umpire must cover all converging fly balls

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 should have the first opportunity to go out, since U2 should allow U1 or U3 the first opportunity and only go out if neither does

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire's initial angle on a developing tag play is poor, but the umpire moves purposefully to a better angle as the throw arrives. Which technique described in Appendix 4 does this reflect, and what is its purpose?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Active feet, used solely to maintain balance while standing still

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The mental snapshot technique, in which the umpire takes a mental photograph from the initial angle, then a second from the improved angle, combining them into a clearer 3D picture of the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax correction, which eliminates the need to change position

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The leading edge principle, which requires the umpire to remain at 90 degrees to the runner's path at all times

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A Base Umpire in a 3- or 4-umpire system must decide whether to go out on a fly ball. One available position is closer to the play but offers a compromised sightline; another is farther away but offers a clean, unobstructed angle. Which choice reflects Appendix 4's stated principle for outfield coverage decisions?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The farther position with the clean angle, because in all cases angles take priority over distance

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The closer position, because proximity always produces the most accurate judgment

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Neither position; the umpire should request a video review

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The closer position, because distance takes priority over angle in outfield coverage

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A developing umpire treats their textbook starting position at second base as the position from which every call must be made, even as a throw and tag pull the play toward the leading edge. Which key principle from Appendix 4 does this approach fail to reflect?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Primary Responsibilities, because the umpire must always rotate to another base first

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Dynamic Positioning and Adjustments, because there is no 'X marks the spot' position - starting and observation positions must never be assumed to be the final calling position

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Pre-Pitch Preparation and Outfield Coverage, because the umpire failed to anticipate outfielder depth

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax Error, because the umpire was aligned with the wrong plane

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What is the 'mental snapshot' technique described in Appendix 4?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Count the pitches in each at-bat

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Memorise the batter's stance before each pitch

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Take a photograph with a phone after the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Take a mental photograph of the play from the initial angle, move quickly to a better angle, take a second photograph, and combine them into a clearer 3D picture

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Good judgement comes from gathering as much visual information as possible; obtaining the correct angle often matters more than physical proximity.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which sequence does Appendix 4 give for good timing on a play?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.11.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Signal, see the play, decide, stop

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: See the play, signal, decide, process the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Stop, see the play, process the play, decide, signal

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Decide, stop, signal, see the play

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Preparing the signal before the play is complete shifts the brain's focus away from the final elements of the action and encourages early calling.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 4, what is the risk of focusing only on the tag action?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire will move too early to the leading edge

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire will lose track of the count

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The brain may prematurely 'affirm' an out because it sees the glove contact the runner, overriding the relationship between the ball, runner and base, such as the runner already touching the base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire will see the ball too well

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Poor angle or parallax combined with affirmation bias increases the likelihood of an incorrect call; when the eyes are not aligned with the play, the brain fills in missing information, often incorrectly.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Under Appendix 4, when can the umpire near second base call an illegal pitch for the pitcher's stepping foot?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Only when the plate umpire asks

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Whenever the foot touches the edge of the lane

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Only in the first inning

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: When the stepping foot lands wholly outside the pitching lane and the violation is clear and obvious

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Only the stepping foot must land within the pitching lane. The standard for enforcement is clear and obvious; the adjustment to see it is temporary and must not compromise primary responsibilities.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 4, who can accurately judge whether a deep fly ball passes inside or outside the foul pole?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The plate umpire from behind the catcher

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire on the foul line with an unobstructed view of the foul pole

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Any umpire inside the diamond

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire near second base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Adding distance, or viewing from inside the diamond, increases parallax error; an umpire near second base is at an angle that distorts the judgement.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: From the slot, which parts of the strike zone does Appendix 4 say the plate umpire sees most clearly?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The inside and the top; the outside corner and the bottom are harder to judge

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The outside and the bottom; the inside and the top are harder to judge

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Only the middle of the plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: All parts equally

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The plate umpire's eyes are aligned with the inside and top planes; for the outside and low pitches the pitcher's release point and the catcher's glove movement give additional inputs.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.16.q
Foundations Learning Guide: How far behind second base is the standard starting position for U2 or U3 at second base, according to Appendix 4?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: On the base itself

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Approximately 3-4 m (10-12 ft), within the area formed by the Second Base Diagonal Angle and the extension of the third base line

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Approximately 8-10 m (26-33 ft) directly behind the base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: About 1 m (3 ft), beside the base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: This position establishes a proactive observation point and lets the umpire move efficiently around the base; starting further away increases the movement arc.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 4, on which hits must a base umpire in a 3- or 4-umpire system go out?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Only hits that go over the fence

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Only when the plate umpire asks

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Any hit that could be caught by an outfielder in their coverage area, requires a fair/foul decision in the outfield, or could be a home run

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Only hits that are caught

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: In all cases angles take priority over distance.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a Four-Umpire system, what does U2 do when U1 goes out on a fly ball toward the right-field area?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Moves inside to cover both first and second base, which reduces the need for a full crew rotation

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Goes out as well

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Stays at second base

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotates to home plate

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 going out on hits to right field improves coverage of the bases closer to home plate.

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a Three-Umpire system with U1 at first base and U3 at third base, how is the outfield divided for going out?

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 takes the whole outfield

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes the whole outfield

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The plate umpire takes all fly balls

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: It is split down the middle: U1 goes out from centre field to the right-field foul line and U3 from centre field to the left-field foul line

m01-mkc.title: m05-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: If an umpire starts at second base the split changes: the plate umpire covers fly balls from the left fielder (or right fielder) to the foul line.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5: Elite Field Mechanics

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentations - Appendix 5, Part A: Key Concepts

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In Appendix 5a's Four Essential Element Theory (FEET), what are the four elements umpires must observe together to make a correct call?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher, the catcher, the batter, and the base umpire

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, the defensive player, the offensive players, and the base or the area of the play

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The strike zone, the runner's lead, the tag, and the fielder's glove

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The starting position, the observation position, the calling position, and the base

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The ball, defensive player, offensive players and base or area of play must be seen together, including control of the ball and the tag/base relationship.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Per Appendix 5a, the Point of Plate (POP) position is located approximately how far behind home plate?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: 1-2 meters (3-6 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: 6-12 meters (20-40 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: 3-5 meters (9-15 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: 2-4 meters (6-12 feet)

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: POP is an area approximately 2-4 meters behind home, not a fixed calling spot. Use it when primary duties permit and adjust as the play develops.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 5a, what does 'Backfilling' refer to?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire clearing the catcher to obtain an unobstructed view of the field

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire moving to the leading edge of a base to judge a tag play

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire counter-rotating to cover a position not filled by another umpire who is required to cover a play elsewhere

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire returning to their between-innings position after a play concludes

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Backfilling counter-rotates an umpire into coverage left vacant because another umpire must cover a play elsewhere. Read the play and communicate.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What does Appendix 5a give as the purpose for use of the Five and Six-Umpire Systems?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: To allow two dedicated outfield umpires to cover fly-ball responsibilities so the remaining umpires can stay in the infield and cover bases at all times

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: To replace the Plate Umpire with two additional outfield umpires

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To eliminate the need for any rotations between bases

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: To allow all umpires to officiate exclusively from foul territory

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Dedicated outfield coverage allows the remaining umpires to maintain infield/base coverage, particularly at third and home. This purpose is stated in Appendix 5a itself; detailed system mechanics are not assessed here.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What is the purpose of the holding position described in Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: To provide a flexible observation area in foul territory from which the umpire reads which base, 3B or HP, needs coverage and can move to that base.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: To replace all rotation responsibilities with a fixed calling spot.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To keep U1 waiting near first instead of completing a required rotation home.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: To keep the plate umpire in a position where he can make a call at both bases from a distance.

m01-mkc.title: m06-mkc.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The holding position is an oval area that permits active observation and adjustment. It can be nearer the likely play while still allowing movement to the other base if needed.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5a: Key Concepts

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentation - Appendix 5b: Three-Umpire System

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: You are set to judge a force play when the fielder leaves the base to catch an errant throw and attempts a swipe tag. What should you do?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the original view and judge only whether the throw arrived first.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Watch only the runner because the ball and fielder's possession can be assumed peripherally.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the change in the play, use controlled adjustment to see the ball-glove, tag, runner and base relationship, and judge the complete play as all elements come together before signaling.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly over the base to shorten the view as angle is preferred over distance.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: A developing tag can require a different angle from the initial force-play view. Preserve sight of all four elements, including control and the base touch, rather than assuming the original calling position remains sufficient.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: According to Appendix 5a, when does parallax error most commonly occur?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax error is mainly caused by distance. Moving closer improves judgment regardless of the angle, provided the umpire can see the runner and fielder.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: An unsuitable viewing angle can distort the relationship between the runner, base and tag point. Greater distance can compound this, with straight-lining of all the elements causing the greatest loss of visual separation.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax error occurs only when the elements are completely straight-lined. Until then, the umpire can accurately judge the sequence without adjusting their position.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Remaining stationary at the original observation position prevents parallax error. Moving during the play changes the perspective and makes the sequence less reliable, even when the original view becomes partly blocked.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Parallax error can affect judgment before the umpire becomes completely straight-lined. An unsuitable angle can distort the apparent relationship between the runner, base and tag point, and greater distance can compound the problem. Straight-lining is particularly dangerous because the elements overlap, reducing depth perception and potentially hiding whether the runner touched the base before the tag. Use the leading edge when it provides the required view, and adjust purposefully to maintain an unobstructed angle and visual separation.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire wants to remove parallax error on a fair/foul call. What does Appendix 5a say they should do?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stand as far back as possible to see the whole field

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Rely on the base umpire to make the call

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait for the ball to stop before deciding

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Position themselves on the plane of the call, such as on the fair/foul line

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: For a fair/foul decision, move onto the relevant fair/foul line so the ball can be judged against that plane directly. Additional timing and angle adjustments may still be needed for other elements of the play.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second, the umpire working 2BDA may need to cover first if U1 goes out. Which starting choice does Appendix 5a prefer?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Start on the 1B side and/or be ready to move toward the first-base side of 2BDA, maintaining an unobstructed view of home and the batter, so the umpire can move inside promptly for possible first-base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the third-base-side alternate position to obtain the best angle on a possible pickoff at second, then move across the diamond if first-base coverage becomes necessary.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Start farther behind second on 2BDA to obtain a wider view of the outfield, accepting the additional movement needed to establish a calling position at first.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Start toward the third-base-line extension to prioritise the runner advancing to third, leaving U1 responsible for first until the outfield play is completed.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second, starting on 1B side, the preferred side or slightly toward the first-base side of 2BDA helps the umpire move inside and cover first if U1 goes out. The position must still provide an unobstructed view of home and the batter and allow the umpire to establish the required angle and distance for the developing play. U2 does not then have to worry about the runners lead off from 2B.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a play, what distance from the base does Appendix 5a give for a force play and for a tag play?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3 m (10 ft) for a force play and 5 m (16 ft) for a tag play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5 m (16 ft) for a force play and 3 m (10 ft) for a tag play

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5 m (16 ft) for both

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3 m (10 ft) for both

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5a gives approximately 5 meters for a force play and 3 meters for a tag play. These are working distances, not the separate before-pitch starting distances. Angle takes priority when angle and distance cannot both be ideal; retain room to adjust and reach the leading edge.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 needs to come inside to cover multiple bases and remain able to adapt to a late going-out decision or backfill. Which technique follows Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Enter the diamond and button-hook by turning around the left shoulder, retaining the view and flexibility for the required coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the right foot planted at first and twist only the upper body.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the ball into the outfield without checking the runner or crew.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay in foul territory even when that prevents covering the required base.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Button-hooking turns around the left shoulder after entering the diamond. It supports multiple-base coverage and adaptation to a changed rotation, backfill or a partner's late decision. U2 also uses it in the four-umpire example when U1 goes out.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Why does Appendix 5a say an umpire must never position directly over a base when making a call?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: It places the umpire too close to follow the throw into the glove, so the calling position should remain at force-play distance even when a tag develops.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: It prevents the umpire from maintaining a 90-degree angle to the throw, which must be held throughout both force and tag plays.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: It limits the umpire’s view of secondary plays, so the calling position should prioritise the next possible throw rather than the tag and base touch.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: It vertically aligns the umpire’s eyes with the base, causing the ball, tag and leading edge to overlap, reducing depth perception and making their timing harder to judge.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Calling directly over the base can collapse the elements into a straight-lined view. This reduces visual separation and may distort whether the runner touched the base before the tag. A position just short of the leading edge, with appropriate angle, depth and adjustment, helps the umpire see the elements come together clearly.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A ball is hit to the outfield and no umpire goes out. U2 can keep all Four Essential Elements in front from outside. Which statement correctly applies Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Every Base Umpire must remain outside whenever no umpire goes out.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 must call time before choosing a position.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 may stay outside in that circumstance; if an umpire goes out, the remaining Base Umpires must come inside for coverage and backfill.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 may stay outside even when a partner goes out and inside coverage is needed.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Coming inside is the usual response to the ball in the outfield. Section 5a expressly allows U2 to remain outside if all four elements stay in front and nobody goes out. Any umpire going-out situation requires the remaining Base Umpires to come inside for coverage and in particular backfilling.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the four-umpire backfill example, U2 or U3 goes out and the Plate Umpire communicates that they are staying at home for a play. What should the remaining Base Umpires do?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining U2 or U3 umpire covers third; U1 works inside to cover first and second if possible, with an alternative position and crew adjustment if moving inside would interfere with play.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Both remaining Base Umpires stay at second until the play at home ends.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Order the Plate Umpire to leave home for third even though the play is at home.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Require U1 to enter the diamond even if doing so interferes with a runner or throw.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire's home-coverage communication triggers this example. The remaining U2/U3 backfills third. If U1 cannot enter without interference, U1 moves toward the fence near the first-base dugout and the partner stays aware of possible second-base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a close force play where the runner reaches the base and then the fielder receives the throw, an umpire who watches the throw or rushes the call is most likely to make what error, per Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner safe

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Call the runner out, because they are still processing the throw being caught

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Call interference

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Fail to see the base

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner is safe in the stated sequence, but a rushed umpire may react to the later catch and call out. A slight pause allows all inputs to be processed in order before deciding and communicating.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 is required to rotate home while the lead runner advances. Which approach follows Appendix 5a's home-coverage priority?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Wait in the former first-base holding area until the runner has reached first.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stop at the third-base-line extension for every potential swipe tag.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Release first without observing the required tag-up or base touch and leave the crew to guess the rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Complete the required first-base observation even if looking over the shoulder, release promptly, communicate to push the Plate Umpire toward third, and move toward POP without an unnecessary holding-area delay.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Lead-runner and home coverage have priority. Observe required tag-ups and the batter-runner's touch of first, including over the right shoulder when appropriate, then rotate promptly. The old U1 first-base holding area is omitted and only a reference point because it delays home coverage. POP is a flexible observation reference, not a fixed final call.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What does Appendix 5a mean by 'active feet'?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.11.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire jogs in place between pitches to stay warm

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire takes quick small steps while the ball is in the air

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire moves both feet when adjusting position so they stay balanced on the balls of their feet and ready to move

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire keeps one foot planted until the call is made

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Move both feet when possible to remain balanced on the balls of the feet and ready to adjust. This does not mean moving unnecessarily: remain stationary if the view is stable and clear; adjust when the view into the tag narrows or is blocked, keeping the head and eyes controlled.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: An umpire is considering the alternate starting position at second rather than the preferred side of 1B side of the 2BDA. They must account for the batter’s handedness and the pitcher’s exit path, which may block the view of the batter and plate area. Which description correctly identifies when and where this alternate may be used?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first or runners on first and third, about 3.5 meters back on the first-base side of 2BDA, providing a direct route inside for first-base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on second or runners on second and third, about 3.5 meters back in the third-base-side alternate area, prioritising a view of the runner returning to second.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first or runners on first and third, about 3.5 meters back, just off 2BDA on the third-base side, provided the batter and home remain visible and access to the leading edge and required inside coverage is preserved.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first or runners on first and third, about 3.5 meters back toward the first-base-line extension, using the base as the alignment reference for the anticipated tag.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The alternate is conditional, not the preferred default. Use it within the stated runner configurations when it provides an unobstructed view of home and the batter. Check the sightline for both left- and right-handed batters, including the effect of the pitcher’s exit path. The umpire must remain able to adjust toward 2BDA, reach the leading edge, or move inside to cover first if U1 goes out. They must not move farther toward the first-base-line extension.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: From the third-base-side alternate at second, why must the umpire avoid moving farther right toward the extension of the line from first through second?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: It can put the base between the umpire and the play, increasing parallax and obscuring the runner’s contact with the base. Movement should preserve access toward 2BDA and 1B side at the leading edge.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: It takes the umpire away from a 90-degree angle to the catcher’s throw, which should remain the primary alignment throughout the tag attempt.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: It increases the distance from the tag point, so the umpire should move directly toward the base rather than adjust the viewing angle as the play develops.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: It moves the umpire outside the standard starting area, which must be maintained until the tag is completed before adjusting for a secondary play.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The alternate already places the umpire on the third-base side of 2BDA. Moving farther toward 1BLE can place the base between the umpire and the tag, reducing visual separation and distorting whether the runner remains in contact with the base. Read the play and move toward 2BDA in the first instance, then adjust toward the first-base side or leading edge as required. The priority is an unobstructed view of the elements, rather than a fixed angle to the throw or remaining within a starting area.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: On a passed ball or wild pitch, the Plate Umpire is not required to rotate toward third and a runner advances home. Which movement follows Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move left automatically without reading the catcher's retrieval movement, then remain fixed.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay directly behind the catcher throughout the retrieval and tag attempt.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move immediately onto the third-base-line extension for every play.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the catcher's shoulders, clear to allow retrieval, find the ball, avoid the throwing lane, and establish an observation and calling position that preserves all four elements; clearing may be left or right.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The usual initial left movement has exceptions. On a passed ball or wild pitch without a required third-base rotation or coverage, clear according to the catcher's turn, then read and adjust for the play at home. Avoid 3BLE when it places the plate between you and the runner.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which approach best describes the information an umpire should consider in Pre-Pitch Preparation (PPP) under Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Review the count, outs, runner positions and assigned coverage, then use standard rotation patterns without adjusting the preparation for individual players’ speed, range or throwing ability.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Combine the count, outs and score with runners’ speed and advancement potential, outfielders’ depth and throwing arms, and fielders’ capabilities to anticipate likely plays while remaining ready to adapt.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Identify the most likely play from the defensive alignment, then commit to its calling position before contact so the umpire arrives ahead of the runner and throw.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Prioritise the lead runner’s speed and the nearest fielder’s position, leaving assessment of other runners, outfield depth and secondary-play possibilities until the ball is hit.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: PPP combines the correct starting setup with knowledge of the game situation and players’ capabilities. Consider the count, outs, score, runners’ speed and intentions, outfield positioning and arms, and fielders’ range and ability to execute a play. Use that information to anticipate possibilities and adapt quickly. Anticipating a play does not mean committing to its outcome or moving early to a predetermined calling position.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.16.q
Foundations Learning Guide: What should a base umpire do before deciding to go out on a fly ball, according to Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the outfielders’ starting positions to select coverage immediately on contact, then confirm the ball’s flight and communicate once moving into the outfield.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the ball’s initial direction and commit if it enters their coverage area, leaving partners to adjust from observing the umpire’s movement.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the flight and the outfielders’ reactions, but give the umpire at 2B the first opportunity because the central position provides the widest coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the ball’s flight and catch potential, check partners’ movements and coverage priorities, then communicate before committing to go out.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Watch the actual flight before committing. Pre-pitch knowledge of outfielder depth and ability supports the decision but does not replace reading the ball. Check partners and communicate. The corner umpire has the first option over the umpire at second; with both corners occupied in the three-umpire example, U1 has first option. Go out when the play requires it within the assigned coverage, while avoiding unnecessary movement that weakens base or home-plate coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A routine hit has clearly landed and is bounding in the outfield, with no catch, fair/foul or home-run judgment requiring you to go out. Multiple runners are advancing. What should you do?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue into the outfield to confirm how the ball is fielded, leaving the remaining umpires to expand their base coverage until the ball returns.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move toward the outfielder to establish a better angle on the return throw, then recover toward the bases once the defense selects its play.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the required base coverage, remain visually connected with the ball and runners, and avoid an unnecessary going-out movement.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the ball beyond the bases until the outfielder gains control, then decide which base requires coverage from the direction of the throw.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Once the ball has clearly landed and no outfield judgment requires going out, maintain the assigned base coverage and prepare for advancing runners and secondary plays. Keep the ball and runners in view, read the developing throw, and adjust to obtain the required angle and distance. Unnecessary going out can weaken coverage, particularly at third and home.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: After completing the outfield judgment, the umpire who went out looks back and sees a nearby base uncovered because of a missed rotation, with a play about to occur. What may that umpire do under Appendix 5a?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Return to cover that empty location if needed and clearly communicate the responsibility to the crew, or provide what was observed if the controlling umpire requests information.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Return automatically and take over the base not covered by another umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Make an infield call without telling the crew that the coverage has changed.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Ignore the uncovered play because the umpire has gone out, this ends all BU duties.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: This is a specific elite correction for missing coverage, not routine drift back into an occupied area. The umpire who goes out must look back and observe infield plays. Clear communication such as "I'm here" and the umpire's name tells partners the empty location has been covered.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: All plays have concluded and U1 is at home. What releases the crew to counter-rotate to the positions for the next pitch?

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The pitcher holding the ball securely in the circle and all runners returning to their bases, allowing each umpire to begin moving independently.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 at home calling time, followed by coordinated counter-rotation so the incoming umpire takes control before the outgoing umpire releases the area.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 or U3 beginning the return toward their starting position, prompting U1 and the Plate Umpire to follow once they recognise the movement.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire initiating the return toward home, with the base umpires adjusting as that movement creates space for the counter-rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m06-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: When all plays have concluded and U1 is at home, U1 calls time to release the crew for counter-rotation. The return is coordinated: an umpire retains responsibility until released by the incoming umpire taking control. Possession in the pitcher’s circle alone does not initiate this sequence, and leaving early can create an uncovered base.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5b: Three-Umpire System

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentation - Appendix 5b: Three-Umpire System

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners on, which U3 starting position follows Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 meters behind third, up to 2 meters off the line in foul territory.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5.5 meters behind third, just off the line in foul territory.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About 4.5 meters behind third, just off the line in foul territory.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 meters back near 2BDA, on the first-base side of second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The no-runner reference is about 5.5 meters behind third, just off the line. The other distances and locations relate to different runner configurations. Depth is approximate and must permit timely movement and a clear view.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 starts near 2BDA and reads a pickoff at second. Which description follows the pickoff guidance?

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move backward about 3 meters from the starting position before reading the tag.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Hold the starting position throughout because 2BDA is the final calling spot.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Adjust to a position about 3 meters from the base, keeping the Four Essential Elements in view as the tag develops.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move onto the first-base-line extension before the throw arrives to prepare for every swipe tag.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3 meters describes the working distance from the base, not a prescribed three-meter backward movement. Read the runner and fielder and adjust for an unobstructed view. The PDF heading identifies U3 although the sentence beneath it mistakenly says U2.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a three umpire system with runner 1B and 3B. Which allocation of lead-off responsibility follows Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes first, U3 takes second and the Plate Umpire takes third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The umpire nearest each runner takes that runner regardless of the assigned position.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes first and second; U3 takes third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes first, and the Plate Umpire takes second and third while U3 reads the outfield.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The leadoff allocation is U1 at first and second, U3 at third. Do not confuse leaving early on the pitch with tag-up responsibilities on a caught fly ball.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a three umpire system with a runner on first, U1 at first and U3 at second, why is U1 assigned the right-field area, including some balls directly behind U3?

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 has a useful right-field line/trap angle on balls that come to the line, while U3 can enter more easily to cover bases and the tag-up without U1 button-hooking across the runner's path.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 must remain outside at second throughout the play, so U1 takes the ball mainly to avoid changing U3's initial viewing angle.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 going out removes all first-base responsibilities from the crew until the ball is returned to the infield.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1's deeper route gives priority over U3 on every outfield ball.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The allocation combines useful line and trap-ball angles with efficient base coverage. U3 can enter the diamond, watch the tag-up and cover first/second more readily than U1 can time a button hook around the runner.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A Base Umpire goes out and the fly ball is not caught. Who takes the batter-runner around to third in the elite three-umpire system?

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The Plate Umpire takes the batter-runner through third while the remaining Base Umpire takes 1B and 2B.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining Base Umpire takes the batter-runner through third, communicating so the Plate Umpire can cover home.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The outfield umpire returns to third after ruling on the catch while the remaining Base Umpire stays at second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining Base Umpire stops coverage at second and transfers every third-base play to the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m07-mkc.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining Base Umpire covers first and second and takes the batter-runner to third. For a caught fly ball, taking the last runner to third depends on reaching an advantageous position and communicating with the Plate Umpire.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5c & d: Four, Five and Six-Umpire Systems

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentation - Appendix 5c & d: Four, Five and Six-Umpire Systems

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which plate-meeting arrangement follows the Four-Umpire System?

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: PU behind the boxes, with the Base Umpires arranged U1, U2, U3 from the first-base line toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU behind the boxes, with the Base Umpires behind PU in the order they will rotate around the bases.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU behind the boxes at the point of the plate, with U2, U1 and U3 in front of the boxes from the first-base side toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: PU in front of the boxes facing the catcher, with all Base Umpires on the third-base side.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The stated U2, U1, U3 arrangement in front of the boxes allows the crew to peel off to their assigned starting positions. PU remains behind the boxes at the point of the plate.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner at first, which U1 start follows the four-umpire guidance?

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5.5 meters behind first, using the no-runner depth for every runner configuration.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 meters behind first in foul territory, maintaining a view of the pitcher, runner, batter and home.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About 4.5 meters behind first in fair territory, aligned with the second baseman.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 meters back at 2BDA, allowing U2 to take the first-base playback.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner-at-first reference is approximately 3.5 meters behind the base in foul territory. Keep the home-plate view clear and remain ready to adjust for the runner's return or a developing tag.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 goes out on a fly ball. Which crew allocation includes the correct third-base tag-up responsibility?

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 watches first and third while PU watches the catch only.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 keeps third while U1 watches first and second.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 watches third from the outfield while U3 moves inside.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: PU watches third, U3 watches second and U1 watches first.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 rotates to second, including its tag-up. PU has the third-base tag-up while U1 retains first. The movement and tag-up responsibilities must be coordinated.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A fly ball could be taken by U2 or the appropriate corner umpire. Which approach follows the four-umpire coverage priority?

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 commits first because the central starting position gives U2 priority over either corner.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 reads the ball and allows U1 or U3 the first option within their coverage, then communicates and goes if the corner umpire does not take it.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU selects the going-out umpire after the ball reaches the outfielder.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both umpires go out initially and the one farther from the ball returns to the bases.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Corner priority combines useful line and pole angles with efficient base coverage. Reading the ball and partners before committing helps avoid overlapping coverage and unnecessary rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners or only a runner on first, which PU movement follows an infield hit in the four-umpire system?

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate immediately to third as soon as the batter-runner leaves the box.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay fixed at POP and transfer all first-base-area interference observations to U1.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Trail about one-third toward first for the required observations and fair/foul decision, then return home when the batter-runner reaches first.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Trail the batter-runner through first and second before releasing home coverage to U3.

m01-mkc.title: m08-mkc.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The infield-play instruction is to trail for possible interference, tag or assistance, while retaining fair/foul responsibility, then return home as the batter-runner reaches first. Other runner configurations use POP.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5b: Three-Umpire System

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: Continue to Presentation - Appendix 5c & d: Four, Five and Six-Umpire Systems

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which complete between-inning arrangement follows Appendix 5b, with all umpires standing off the fair/foul lines?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: PU one-third toward third; U1 halfway toward first; U3 two-thirds toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU halfway toward third; U1 one-third toward first; U3 two-thirds toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU one-third toward third; U1 two-thirds toward first; U3 halfway toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: PU one-third toward first; U1 halfway toward first; U3 two-thirds toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The specified arrangement is PU one-third up the third-base side, U1 halfway up the first-base side, and U3 two-thirds up the third-base side, all off the lines.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first only, which U1 starting position follows Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 meters behind first and 2-3 meters off the line in foul territory, using the same lateral offset as U3 with a runner on third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: About 5.5 meters behind first, just off the line in foul territory.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 meters behind first in foul territory, near the line with an unobstructed view of home and readiness for a playback.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: About 3.5 meters back on the third-base side of 2BDA, using the alternate second-base setup.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 starts about 3.5 meters behind first in foul territory. The line-side position supports a quick playback and fair/foul coverage. U1 may adjust slightly for a clear home-plate view; U3's wider third-base offset is not automatically copied at first.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Why may U3 start about 3.5 meters behind third and up to 2 meters off the line in foul territory when a runner is on third?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: To align directly with the catcher's throw and keep that fixed alignment throughout any pickoff, even when the tag moves.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: To establish an earlier route to second and release third before the runner commits toward home.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: To obtain one close calling position that can be held for every possible tag without further adjustment.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: To retain a view of the pitcher, runner, batter and home even when the runner leads into foul territory and would screen a line-side position.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The offset protects U3's view through the pitch and lead-off, especially when a runner leads widely in foul territory. U3 reads the runner's return and fielder's tag and adjusts rather than holding a fixed calling spot.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Starting at first, U1 reads a pickoff throw back to the base. Which positioning approach follows Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the approximately five-meter force-play distance and remain at 90 degrees to the throw even if the fielder attempts a swipe tag.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Start just off the fair foul line and work to about 3 meters in foul territory without passing a 45-degree line through first, or step into fair territory when the leading-edge play requires that view.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to the first-base-line extension before reading the runner's return, using the same position for every playback.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move directly beside the fielder's glove and use the ball's arrival to determine whether the runner is out.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the runner's path and fielder's action. The guide permits a foul-territory angle within the stated limit or a step inside for a leading-edge view. The objective is to see the tag and base contact together.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: One Base Umpire goes out on an outfield fly ball. Which statements correctly describe tag-up coverage?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.s0
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining Base Umpire is responsible for tag-ups at first and second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.s1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU is responsible for the tag-up at third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.s2
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining Base Umpire should rotate inside promptly and glance over the shoulder when needed to observe first touch and the runner.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.s3
Foundations Learning Guide: If the required relationship was not seen, the crew should seek assistance and clearly identify the umpire with the relevant observation.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1 and 2 only.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1, 3 and 4 only.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 2, 3 and 4 only.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: All four statements.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: All four are correct. Remaining inside coverage is divided so the Base Umpire watches first/second tag-ups and PU watches third. If a rotation prevents seeing first touch and the runner together, use partner information and communicate who has the observation; do not infer it.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A runner starts on second and U3 is stationed at third. Which umpire has the lead-off call as the pitch is delivered?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1, because the leadoff allocation assigns first and second to U1 and third to U3.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3, because the separate tag-up exception at second also transfers every leadoff there.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU, because the Plate Umpire sees the pitching release most directly.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 and U3 jointly, with whichever signals first controlling the decision.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 has the second-base lead-off responsibility. A leadoff on the pitch and a tag-up on a caught fly ball are different observations with different allocation provisions; the tag-up exception does not change this leadoff assignment.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners, U1 at first and U3 at third, a fly ball takes the normally positioned center fielder toward right field. Which coverage is correct?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 takes the catch because the center fielder began within U3's normal central sector, while U1 holds first.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes the fly ball toward right; U3 moves inside and reads the movement and prepares the remaining base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU takes the catch whenever the center fielder moves, with both Base Umpires retaining their starting bases.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 and U3 both go out until the fielder establishes which side of center will make the catch.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: From the corner starts, U1 covers the normally positioned center fielder moving toward right and the right-field foul sector. U3 covers center toward left. Read flight and partners and communicate before committing.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first, U1 at first and U3 at second, a fly ball takes the left fielder toward the left-field foul line. Who takes the fair/foul and catch/no-catch decisions?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 takes both decisions because U3 is the umpire designated for the third-base side.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes both decisions by crossing the central coverage area, leaving U3 to cover first.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU takes both decisions in the open left-field-line sector while the Base Umpires maintain the required rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 takes the catch from second while PU takes fair/foul separately, without a coverage handoff.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With U3 starting at second, PU covers the left fielder toward the open left-field foul line. U3 covers the center sector and the left fielder moving toward center. Specifying the fielder's direction avoids the ambiguity of simply saying "to F7."

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners, U1 goes out toward right and a possible play develops on the batter-runner at first. Which initial coverage and handoff follow Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 takes the initial first-base play while PU remains at home throughout.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU moves inside, takes the possible initial play at first, then releases first to U3 as the batter-runner passes first; U3 covers the continued advance and PU prepares third/home coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 returns from the outfield for the first-base play, then goes out again if the ball remains outside.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: PU follows the batter-runner through first, second and third while U3 takes over home.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The no-runner/U1-out case is an exception to a blanket first/second-base allocation. PU handles the possible initial first-base play. U3 rotates inside and assumes first/second after the batter-runner passes first, then takes the batter-runner toward third while PU prepares home.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners and an infield ground ball, which approach correctly combines PU's trailing and coverage duties?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain at POP and leave interference, a possible tag before first and fair/foul to U1.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate immediately to third and transfer all first-base-area observations to U3 before the throw.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Trail the batter-runner to first and keep following toward second even when U3 has rotated there.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Trail about one-third toward first, farther if needed, preserve the fair/foul decision and assistance responsibilities, then rotate toward third if the batter-runner advances toward second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: PU trails for potential interference, a tag nearer home and assistance at first, while retaining fair/foul responsibility. Once the batter-runner reaches first and advances toward second, PU prepares third-base coverage rather than duplicating U3 at second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: PU or U1 is covering home from the POP observation area. Which statements follow the Appendix 5b presentation?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.s0
Foundations Learning Guide: If the catcher already has the ball and the play is at the leading edge, move forward and left as needed to retain the view.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.s1
Foundations Learning Guide: If ball and runner arrive together and a deeper/outside swipe tag develops, adjust forward and right as needed to look into the tag.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.s2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move toward the third-base-line extension before the tag develops, committing early to a swipe-tag position rather than preserving access to the leading edge.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.s3
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the runner's path, ball timing and possible obstruction/interference to read the play, keeping the elements in view as it changes.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1, 2 and 4 only.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1 and 3 only.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 2 and 3 only.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: All four statements.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The catcher's possession, the runner's approach and the ball's arrival help identify the likely contact area. Read and adjust from POP, preserving the view and ability to respond to a change. A rare swipe-tag position is not the routine destination.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first, U3 starts on the first-base side of 2BDA, closer to second. An infield throw creates a force play at second. Which adjustment follows the elite mechanics?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.11.o0
