Foundations Learning Guide: Move right toward 2BDA as the routine response to every play at second, applying the steal-tag movement to the force play and keeping the diagonal as the final calling reference.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move closer along the starting alignment without changing the lateral angle, using proximity to judge possession and base contact even if the fielder screens the runner's arrival.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the throw and move left toward the leading edge, seeking about 90 degrees to the throw and no more than 45 degrees off the leading edge, keeping all four elements visible.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move right toward the first-through-second line extension to center the base in the view, then hold that alignment for the force call before considering a different angle for a subsequent tag.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Being closer to second does not correct a poor angle. From the standard first-base-side start, read the force play and work to your left toward the leading edge. Do not move right automatically on a force play. An adjustment toward 2BDA may suit a developing steal tag, but that is a different play. Keep possession, fielder/base contact and the runner visible, and adjust again if a tag develops.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on first only, U3 selects a second-base starting position considering the batter's handedness, the pitcher's movement and possible first-base coverage if U1 goes out. Which approach is correct?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the third base side alternate as the default because a potential steal always takes priority over the whole-pitch view and first-base access.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the preferred first-base-side standard near 2BDA toward 3BLE, about 3.5 meters back, or the conditional third base side alternate with home unobstructed; when adjustment is needed from the alternate, move toward 2BDA first and retain inside/leading-edge access.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Start toward the first-base-line extension to obtain a swipe-tag view before reading whether the runner attempts a steal or rounds the base.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Start deeper beyond the fielders' range so the pitcher cannot screen the batter, accepting a longer route inside if U1 goes out.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The presentation identifies the first-base-side start as preferred because it preserves the shorter inside route, including first-base coverage. The alternate is conditional, close to 2BDA, and must preserve the view throughout the pitch. From the alternate, initial movement is toward 2BDA, not farther toward 1BLE.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Runners are on first and second, nobody is on third, and neither Base Umpire goes out. PU has a fly ball to the right-field open-line sector. Which tag-up allocation follows the stated exception?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 watches the tag-up at second, while U1 watches first and PU judges the fly ball, with assistance communicated if a required observation is blocked.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 must watch both tag-ups because U1 has the leadoff calls at first and second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU must watch both tag-ups as well as the catch because neither Base Umpire went out.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 watches first while U1 watches second, regardless of their actual sightlines during the rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With first and second occupied and third empty, U3 has the second-base tag-up. The presentation explains that U3 can see that relationship while U1 rotates inside and has first to watch. Leadoff responsibility on the pitch is a separate allocation.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With only a runner on third, U1 at first and U3 at third, an infield ground ball develops. What should U3 do?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate inside as soon as the ball is fielded, leaving PU to take any immediate return to third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain at third until every possible play at first and second has finished, even after the runner commits home.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Retain 3B until the runner commits home, then rotate to second; if U3 remains or is delayed, U1 must cover first and second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Follow the runner to home and require PU to rotate through third toward second.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Do not abandon a runner who can still be played on at third. Once the runner commits home, U3 can release and rotate. U1 reads U3's movement and covers both first and second if U3 cannot release.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners and both Base Umpires on the corners, a ground ball reaches the outfield. Which U1 sequence follows Appendix 5b?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate to POP immediately at contact and leave the initial first-base force possibility to PU.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Button-hook to second and hold all home-plate coverage with PU until the batter-runner stops at third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay behind first throughout, requiring PU to cover the batter-runner at both third and home if the advance continues.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Prepare for an outfield-to-first force play and observe first, then rotate to POP if the batter-runner progresses from second toward third, communicating to push PU toward third.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With no original runners, U1 first protects the possible outfield-to-first play. The batter-runner's advance from second toward third triggers U1's home rotation in this case. Do not apply this timing to a runner-on-first case where the lead runner can threaten home earlier.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.16.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With U1 at first and U3 at third, U3 initially starts out but reads that the ball will not be caught. U1 has begun the inside response. Which recovery follows the Appendix 5b presentation?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 returns to third silently while U1 continues to cover second, third and home until the next pitch.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 takes second without communicating, assuming U1 will notice and change the rotation before the runner arrives.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 continues out solely to preserve the original going-out signal, even though the crew can safely restore better infield coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 clearly communicates visually and verbally that they have second and rotates inside; U1 adjusts the button hook and can proceed toward home, coordinating PU's third base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The correction restores the three-umpire infield rotation and improves coverage around the diamond. The communication is essential because U1 may already have responded to U3's initial movement. Read and coordinate rather than silently reversing the coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: After U3 goes out, U1 is working inside for first and second. At second, which movement approach follows the presentation when the tag location changes?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Mirror the outside 2BDA position from inside and preserve the same angle even if the runner moves away and the fielder screens the tag.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the play and select an inside working lane: toward the third base line for a leading-edge play, or toward the first-base line to look back into a tag developing outside the base.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move closer to the base on a straight line for every tag, relying on distance to compensate for a blocked angle at the side of the base.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Choose the lane from the expected throw before the runner arrives and hold it through the tag, reserving further adjustment for the next play.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Inside positioning has different restrictions from an outside start. Read the likely tag location and use the lane that keeps it in front, then adapt if it changes. These are inside working lanes, not permission to move farther toward 1BLE from the outside third base side alternate. Protect element separation and avoid simply mirroring outside mechanics.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which U3 approach follows the third base pickoff guidance?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain at the initial depth for every playback and use the catcher's throwline as the fixed calling angle.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move immediately to fair territory to the leading edge for every playback, even when the runner returns through foul territory.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the runner's return and fielder's tag, work about 3 meters from third in foul territory and adjust for the required tag or leading-edge view.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move behind the returning runner to align the runner, glove and base, using proximity to establish whether the tag came first.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The runner's return path and fielder's action guide the angle. The foul-territory reference is about 3 meters with the 45-degree limit. Adjust to look into the actual tag; do not assume every return uses the same contact point.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 has gone out on a fly ball. Which U3 response follows the Three-Umpire Rotation Memory Map?

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate inside past the line from the pitcher's plate to second, assume first/second coverage, and be ready to take the batter-runner toward third with clear communication.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Remain outside near 2BDA and cover first and second from there so PU can take every third-base play.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move to the third base holding area and transfer first/second to PU until the outfield ball has been returned.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Hold the third base leading edge for the next throw and leave first uncovered until U1 returns from the outfield.

m01-mkc.title: m07-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The memory map puts U3 inside, past the pitcher to second line, for first and second when U1 goes out. Read the runner and communicate continued third base coverage. With no original runners, the detailed U1-out case gives PU the initial first-base play before U3 assumes it after the batter-runner passes first.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.title
Foundations Learning Guide: Appendix 5c & d: Four, Five and Six-Umpire Systems

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.nextLabel
Foundations Learning Guide: You've completed all eight required modules - view your full assessment record

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which U2 between-inning position is specified for the four-umpire system?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: One-third of the way from home to first, off the line.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Two-thirds of the way from home to third, off the line.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: One-third of the way from home to third, off the line.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Two-thirds of the way from home to first, off the line.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.0.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 uses the first-base side about two-thirds of the way from home to first. U1 is one-third up the same side; PU and U3 use the corresponding thirds on the third-base side.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With a runner on any base, which U2 starting approach follows the four-umpire guidance?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Use approximately 3.5 meters behind second as the reference, adjusting within the approved area for the whole-pitch view and timely access to the required play.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep the no-runner reference of approximately 4.5 meters for every pitch, using the extra depth to see over fielders even when it delays the required inside rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Use approximately 5.5 meters behind second to match both corner umpires' no-runner depth and preserve the same movement arc.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the third-base-side alternate automatically whenever a runner is on any base, even if the pitcher screens home.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.1.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide reduces U2's reference depth from about 4.5 meters with no runners to about 3.5 meters with a runner. These are approximate starts, selected to preserve sightlines and the ability to move inside or adjust to a play. The alternate is conditional, not automatic.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A fly ball goes directly into the normal central-field sector. Neither corner umpire has taken it, and it is not carrying toward a corner's line sector. Who takes the outfield call?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1, because corner priority gives U1 every fly ball regardless of its final coverage sector.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU, because a central-field call should be kept with the umpire behind home.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U2, after reading the flight and partners and clearly communicating the decision to go out.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3, because U2 must remain at second whenever runners are on base.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.2.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 has the central sector. U1 and U3 have first option on appropriate overlapping balls, but that does not transfer every central ball to a corner. Read the actual flight and partners and then be decisive.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 goes out on a fly ball with a runner at first. Which tag-up assignment and reasoning follow the four-umpire system?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 takes the first-base tag-up because U2 will cover first and second after coming inside, combining both tag-up observations with the subsequent calls at those bases.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU takes the first-base tag-up, retaining the required view of the runner and first touch while U2 rotates inside for base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 takes the first-base tag-up from third because the corner-to-corner angle replaces PU's observation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 takes the first-base tag-up while continuing into the outfield, leaving PU responsible only for home.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.3.why
Foundations Learning Guide: PU has the first-base tag-up when U1 goes out. U2 takes second and U3 takes third. A future base-call responsibility does not automatically assign an earlier tag-up when the rotation limits the umpire's view.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With runners on base, U2 goes out. Which remaining-crew tag-up allocation follows Appendix 5c?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 watches first and second while U3 retains third and PU stays solely at home.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU watches first and second while U1 moves home and U3 retains third.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 watches first, U3 rotates to second and watches its tag-up, and PU watches third.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 watches first, U1 watches second and PU watches third, regardless of the initial rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.4.why
Foundations Learning Guide: When U2 goes out, U3 takes second including the tag-up there. U1 retains first and PU takes third. The umpire going out does not continue to judge the infield tag-ups from the outfield.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which statement accurately describes U1's normal route and the response to a backfill in the four-umpire system?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Button-hook inside on every outfield ball before deciding whether to retain first or rotate home, keeping responsibility for first and second even when U2 has already moved inside to cover those bases.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Normally use first-base foul territory or go out, communicate when rotating home and pushing PU toward third; if PU retains home for a quick play, adjust to support the required first/second coverage without interfering.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay at first until all runners stop, because U2's presence removes the need for a home rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate immediately home whenever U2 or U3 starts out, transferring any first-base touch to PU without communication.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.5.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The memory map says U1 does not need a button hook for the normal four-umpire route. That is not an absolute ban on adjusting or working inside during an exceptional backfill. Read PU, communicate and protect the next required coverage without crowding the home play.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.q
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners and no umpire going out, a ground ball reaches left field. Which U2 approach follows the stated left-field case?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Stay outside for the useful angle on the return throw from left, adjusting for a possible play at second while keeping all four of the elements in view.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Button-hook immediately to the same inside position used for every right-field return, keeping the second-base-side angle unchanged even when the left-field throw produces a less open view.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Rotate to third so U3 can take the return throw at second and PU can cover home and first.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move toward first to take its playback and require U1 to take every subsequent second-base call.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.6.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The detailed ground-ball section specifies staying outside for the left-field return angle. Stating no runners also matches the memory-map example. This does not override the inside rotation required when a Base Umpire goes out.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 goes out toward right with runners on second and third. Which remaining-crew coverage best follows Appendix 5c?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 keeps second only, U3 takes first and third by following the batter-runner around the bases, and PU moves toward first to assist while leaving the early home play to U3.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 rotates to second, U2 follows the lead runner to home, and PU takes first and third.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 rotates to third, U3 covers home, and PU takes first and second until the fly ball ends.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 button-hooks inside for first and second, U3 moves to the 3BLE in foul territory and then maintains third-base coverage and adjusts for the play, and PU remains available for the home play from the POP area.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.7.why
Foundations Learning Guide: When U1 goes out, U2 covers first and second and U3 retains third. With the scoring threat from second/third, PU prioritizes home and POP rather than initiating the U2/U3-going-out rotation. This is one reason U1 going out supports efficient coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 goes out. Which comparison correctly distinguishes U1's home-rotation timing with no original runners from the runners-on case?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: With no runners, protect the possible first-base play and start to rotate as the lead runner or batter-runner passes second toward third; with runners on, observe the touch at first and prioritize the earlier home rotation as the lead-runner threat develops.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: In both cases, wait until the batter-runner passes second before rotating home, retaining first-base responsibility for possible return throws while PU divides third and home; the lead runner does not change that release trigger.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: In both cases, rotate home at contact before checking a possible first-base play or the batter-runner's touch.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: In both cases, remain at first until the defense throws to third, then react toward home after PU makes the third-base call.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.8.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The detailed PDF distinguishes the no-runner trigger from runners-on timing. The presentation emphasizes not waiting unnecessarily at first when the lead runner can threaten home; use the shoulder check, communicate, and trust the inside umpire's subsequent first-base coverage.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 has gone out. PU reads a quick play at home before U1 can arrive and communicates that PU is returning home. What coordinated response is required?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 stays at second until PU completes the home call and can return to third, while U1 retains the home rotation because the original assignment remains in force until the play ends.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 continues to POP and shares the home call with PU while U3 waits for the next throw.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: The outfield umpire immediately abandons the fly-ball judgment and takes third without informing the crew.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 backfills third for a subsequent play, while U1 adjusts to support first/second coverage and avoids interfering with the home play; the crew communicates the changed responsibilities.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.9.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The first home play remains the priority. PU's decision triggers the backfill: the remaining U3 fills third, with U1 adjusting as needed for first/second. Do not force a completed home rotation when PU has already taken the call.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.10.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Compare U1 with a runner on first and U3 with a runner on third. Which starting-position approach preserves the view of home and access to the developing tag?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.10.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Both start about 3.5 meters behind their base and 2-3 meters into foul territory, using the same lateral offset because both may face a return throw and tag.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.10.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Both start about 3.5 meters behind their base; U1 stays just off the fair/foul line, while U3 may need more foul-territory offset because the runner leads off in front of U3 rather than away as at first.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.10.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Both start about 3.5 meters behind their base; U1 takes the greater foul-territory offset to look across the returning runner, while U3 stays close to the line to preserve access to the leading edge.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.10.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Both start about 3.5 meters behind their base and use the same lateral offset selected before the pitch, keeping that reference through a return throw so the original observation angle remains consistent.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.10.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The corners are not mirror-image starts. At first, the runner leads away from U1, so U1 starts just off the line in foul territory with an unobstructed view of home. Starting 2-3 meters off the line unnecessarily lengthens the route inside if the tag requires it. At third, the runner can lead in front of U3, so U3 may need a greater foul-territory offset to retain the view of the pitcher, runner, batter and plate. Both read the actual tag and adjust; neither offset is a fixed calling position. The former runner-on-second U3 reference remains approximately 4.5 meters behind third, just off the line.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.11.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 goes out on a fly ball with runners on base. Which tag-up allocation follows Appendix 5c?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.11.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 watches first and second, U2 watches third, and PU takes no tag-up observation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.11.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: PU watches first and second while U1 retains first-base calls and U2 moves toward home.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.11.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 watches first, U2 watches second and PU watches third, with assistance sought if rotation blocks a required observation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.11.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 watches first, PU watches second and U1 watches third, exchanging observations before any appeal while retaining those assignments regardless of the initial inside rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.11.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The remaining crew covers the tag-ups at first, second and third through U1, U2 and PU respectively. Rotating inside does not permit guessing a first-touch or base-contact relationship that was not actually seen.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.12.q
Foundations Learning Guide: R on 2B, U1 goes out on a hard, line drive caught in rightfield. U2 cannot get inside in time to see both first touch and the runner's tag-up at second. What should U2 do?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.12.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Infer the tag-up from the runner's position after the catch and rule without seeking another view.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.12.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Use the sound of the catch while watching the runner and treat that sound alone as proof of the exact first-touch timing.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.12.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Seek U3's observation of the second-base tag-up and communicate the information and action needed before deciding any appeal.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.12.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Keep sole control of the observation even if U3 has a complete view, because assigned coverage prevents crew assistance.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.12.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide expressly allows U2 to seek U3's help in this hard-flat-catch case. Rotate promptly and use a shoulder glance when possible, but if the timing relationship was missed, ask for the actual observation rather than reconstructing it from assumptions.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.13.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a four umpire system, which allocation applies to a runner leaving the base on the pitch in the four-umpire system?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.13.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: PU judges every leadoff because PU has the direct view of the pitcher's delivery.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.13.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 judges first and second while U3 judges third, using the three-umpire allocation so U2 can focus entirely on the central-field sector.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.13.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 judges first and second while U1 and U3 concentrate on their fly-ball sectors.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.13.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Each Base Umpire judges the leadoff at their own base, distinct from any later fly-ball tag-up rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.13.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Four-umpire leadoffs are assigned to the umpire at each base. Do not carry across the three-umpire first/second allocation or confuse a leadoff on the pitch with the separately assigned tag-up on a caught fly ball.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.14.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 starts on the first-base side of 2BDA, closer to second. An infield throw creates a force play at second. Which movement applies the force-play guidance?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.14.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the throw and move left toward the leading edge, seeking about 90 degrees to the throw and no more than 45 degrees off the leading edge, while keeping all four elements visible.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.14.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move right toward 2BDA as the routine response to every play at second, using the steal-tag adjustment for the force play as well and treating the diagonal as the final calling reference.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.14.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Move closer to second along the starting alignment, using the shorter distance to judge possession and base contact while keeping the same lateral angle throughout the force play and any developing tag.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.14.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Move right toward the extension of the line from first through second to bring the base into the center of the view, then judge the force from that alignment before adjusting for a later tag.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.14.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Being closer does not correct a poor angle. From the standard first-base-side start, the presentation shows a move left toward the leading edge for a force play, aiming for about 90 degrees to the throw and no more than 45 degrees off the leading edge. Do not make a routine rightward movement merely because the start is closer to second. A rightward adjustment toward 2BDA may suit an actual steal tag; it is not the default force-play movement. Read the throw, fielder, runner and base contact, and adjust again if a tag develops or the view becomes obstructed.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.15.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A runner starts on second and U1 goes out to rightfield. PU has home coverage and is observing from POP, but the throw and tag have not yet developed. Which approach preserves the required home view?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.15.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Move early toward the third-base-line extension to prepare for a swipe tag, then use that position for the first home play before considering whether the leading edge would provide a clearer view.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.15.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Use POP to track the ball, runner and fielder; read the timing of the throw and runner then the potential developing tag before adjusting, preserving access to the leading edge rather than committing early toward the third base line extension(3BLE).

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.15.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Choose the leading edge as the final calling position before the throw develops, then hold that spot through the play because reaching the leading edge removes the need for further lateral adjustment.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.15.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Use POP until the throw starts, then follow the ball toward the third-base-line extension regardless of the runner and catcher, using the incoming throw as the sole reference for the final tag angle.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.15.why
Foundations Learning Guide: With U1 out, PU retains home while U2 covers first/second and U3 covers third. POP is an observation area, not a commitment to a predetermined tag angle. Track the runner for possible obstruction or interference and read the throw and fielder. Moving prematurely toward 3BLE can put the plate between the umpire and runner, obscure the tag or touch, and make a return to the leading edge difficult. Move left toward the leading edge or make another necessary adjustment as the actual play develops. A small rightward adjustment may reveal a swipe tag; it does not justify an early move all the way toward 3BLE.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.16.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 goes out. Before U1 reaches home, PU returns from the holding zone for the first play at the plate and communicates the backfill. Who takes the subsequent third-base coverage?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.16.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: U1 must leave the first-base side and cross directly to third, while U2 retains only second.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.16.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 backfills third, while U1 adjusts to support first/second coverage without crowding PU's home play.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.16.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: PU must finish the home call and then sprint to third, because U2 can never leave second.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.16.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 must return from the outfield for every third-base play, regardless of whether the crew can communicate a safe handoff.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.16.why
Foundations Learning Guide: When U3 is out, U2 is the remaining inside Base Umpire who can backfill third after PU takes home. U1 reads the changed coverage and avoids unnecessary movement into the play. Crew awareness and communication protect both the first and next play.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.q
Foundations Learning Guide: Which statements correctly describe U2's starting choices and movement from the third-base-side alternate?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.s0
Foundations Learning Guide: The preferred standard start is on the first-base side between 2BDA and the third base line extension, with depth adjusted to the runners.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.s1
Foundations Learning Guide: The third-base-side alternate is conditional, with a runner on first or runners on first and third; check batter handedness and the pitcher's landing/exit, keeping home unobstructed and the required first-base route available.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.s2
Foundations Learning Guide: When adjustment is needed from the alternate, move toward 1B and 2BDA first rather than farther toward the first base line extension (1BLE), which can put the base between the umpire and the runner/tag and obscure base contact.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.s3
Foundations Learning Guide: For a force play, continue toward the required leading-edge angle, crossing 2BDA if needed; if all elements are already clear, movement to the leading edge is not required merely for its own sake.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1 and 2 only.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 2 and 3 only.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1, 3 and 4 only.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: All four statements.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.17.why
Foundations Learning Guide: All four are correct. The standard first-base-side position remains preferred; the alternate is conditional. From the alternate, do not move farther toward 1BLE. That can put the base between the umpire and the runner/tag, increasing parallax and obscuring contact with the base. When an adjustment is required, move toward 2BDA first and continue toward the required leading-edge view as the play dictates. On a force play this may require crossing 2BDA to gain about 90 degrees to the throw and no more than 45 degrees off the leading edge. An existing clear view does not require movement for its own sake.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.18.q
Foundations Learning Guide: A free runner advances from second toward third and the fielder prepares a tag. Which U3 approach follows the guide and presentation?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.18.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Commit to the third-base-line (3BLE) extension before the runner arrives, treating that as the final position for every swipe tag.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.18.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Move straight to the leading edge before reading the runner's slide or fielder's receiving position, then hold that angle through the tag because reaching the leading edge completes the required positioning.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.18.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Read the runner's path and fielder, use a foul-territory observation position when it gives the view, and adjust toward the leading edge or other required tag angle as the play develops.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.18.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Judge the tag from the original starting depth and use the timing of the ball entering the glove as the deciding event.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.18.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The guide permits foul territory when it provides an unobstructed look into the tag. It is an observation choice, not a fixed destination. Retain access to the leading edge and adjust to the actual point of contact and base touch.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.19.q
Foundations Learning Guide: U2 has gone out, runners were already on base, and U1 releases first to rotate home while PU prepares third. Which coverage must U3 now maintain?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.19.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Inside coverage of second and the runner released at first, with readiness to backfill third if PU instead returns home for a quick play.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.19.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Second only, because U1 retains first-base responsibility even while working home; U3 should delay any first-base adjustment until U1 completes the home call and signals a transfer.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.19.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Third only, because first and second transfer to PU once U1 starts toward home.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.19.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: Home alongside U1, leaving the next first/second play until U2 returns from the outfield.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.19.why
Foundations Learning Guide: U3 rotates inside when U2 goes out and picks up the runner released by U1 at first as well as second-base coverage. Watch PU and U1: a quick home play taken by PU changes the required third-base coverage and triggers backfill.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.20.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In a six-umpire crew, a deep fly ball is followed by a potential play at a base. Which complete allocation follows Appendix 5d?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.20.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: The appropriate Base Umpire goes out, ULF/URF remain on the lines and the remaining infield crew carries out the full four-umpire rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.20.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: ULF/URF take the fly ball and PU plus two Base Umpires rotate using the three-umpire pattern, leaving the fourth infield umpire as a reserve.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.20.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: ULF/URF take the outfield judgments, no Base Umpire goes out and the infield crew retains its assigned bases without inter-base rotation, while still adjusting position for the view of each play.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.20.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: ULF/URF take the fly ball and all infield umpires hold their exact starting spots because no rotations also prohibits dynamic movement.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.20.why
Foundations Learning Guide: The six-umpire system has PU plus three Base Umpires and two outfield umpires. The outfield pair handles the stated outfield judgments, and there are no base rotations. Each infield umpire still reads and adjusts for angle, separation and the tag at their assigned responsibility.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.q
Foundations Learning Guide: In the six-umpire system, which statements correctly describe the outfield/infield division and ULF/URF technique?

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.s0
Foundations Learning Guide: No Base Umpire goes out, and there are no inter-base rotations; infield umpires still adjust their angles and working positions.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.s1
Foundations Learning Guide: ULF/URF start in front of the outfielders, approximately midway between the Base Umpire and outfielder, up to about one meter inside fair territory near the line with home visible.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.s2
Foundations Learning Guide: If an outfielder runs toward the foul pole, the nearest Base Umpire replaces the outfield umpire and starts the normal four-umpire rotation.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.s3
Foundations Learning Guide: The outfield umpires establish their viewing angle and clearly claim the call; for fair/foul or a pole judgment, use the line and adequate depth, with PU taking fair/foul up to the corner Base Umpire's starting position.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.o0
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1 and 3 only.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.o1
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1, 2 and 4 only.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.o2
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 2, 3 and 4 only.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.o3
Foundations Learning Guide: All four statements.

m01-mkc.title: m08-pca.21.why
Foundations Learning Guide: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Dedicated outfield umpires keep Base Umpires on their assigned infield duties. The outfield start protects the batter view and trap angle; claim the call clearly and use the line and suitable depth for line/pole judgments. A going-out trigger for the Base Umpires is not part of this six-umpire allocation.
